[152](https://docs.rs#152)/// }
[153](https://docs.rs#153)/// ```
[154](https://docs.rs#154)///
[155](https://docs.rs#155)/// See [`#[divan::bench]`](macro@bench) for more examples.
[156](https://docs.rs#156)pub fn main() {
[157](https://docs.rs#157)    Divan::from_args().main();
[158](https://docs.rs#158)}
[159](https://docs.rs#159)
[160](https://docs.rs#160)/// [`black_box`] + [`drop`] convenience function.
[161](https://docs.rs#161)///
[162](https://docs.rs#162)/// # Examples
[163](https://docs.rs#163)///
[164](https://docs.rs#164)/// This is useful when benchmarking a lazy [`Iterator`] to completion with
[165](https://docs.rs#165)/// [`for_each`](Iterator::for_each):
[166](https://docs.rs#166)///
[167](https://docs.rs#167)/// ```
[168](https://docs.rs#168)/// #[divan::bench]
[169](https://docs.rs#169)/// fn parse_iter() {
[170](https://docs.rs#170)///     let input: &str = // ...
[171](https://docs.rs#171)///     # "";
[172](https://docs.rs#172)///
[173](https://docs.rs#173)///     # struct Parser;
[174](https://docs.rs#174)///     # impl Parser {
[175](https://docs.rs#175)///     #   fn new(_: &str) -> Parser { Parser }
[176](https://docs.rs#176)///     #   fn for_each(self, _: fn(&'static str)) {}
[177](https://docs.rs#177)///     # }
[178](https://docs.rs#178)///     Parser::new(input)
[179](https://docs.rs#179)///         .for_each(divan::black_box_drop);
[180](https://docs.rs#180)/// }
[181](https://docs.rs#181)/// ```
[182](https://docs.rs#182)#[inline]
[183](https://docs.rs#183)pub fn black_box_drop<T>(dummy: T) {
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    _ = black_box(dummy);
[185](https://docs.rs#185)}
[186](https://docs.rs#186)
[187](https://docs.rs#187)/// Registers a benchmarking function.
[188](https://docs.rs#188)///
[189](https://docs.rs#189)/// # Examples
[190](https://docs.rs#190)///
[191](https://docs.rs#191)/// The quickest way to get started is to benchmark the function as-is:
[192](https://docs.rs#192)///
[193](https://docs.rs#193)/// ```
[194](https://docs.rs#194)/// use divan::black_box;
[195](https://docs.rs#195)///
[196](https://docs.rs#196)/// #[divan::bench]
[197](https://docs.rs#197)/// fn add() -> i32 {
[198](https://docs.rs#198)///     black_box(1) + black_box(42)
[199](https://docs.rs#199)/// }
[200](https://docs.rs#200)///
[201](https://docs.rs#201)/// fn main() {
[202](https://docs.rs#202)///     // Run `add` benchmark:
[203](https://docs.rs#203)///     divan::main();
[204](https://docs.rs#204)/// }
[205](https://docs.rs#205)/// ```
[206](https://docs.rs#206)///
[207](https://docs.rs#207)/// If benchmarks need to setup context before running, they can take a
[208](https://docs.rs#208)/// [`Bencher`] and use [`Bencher::bench`]:
[209](https://docs.rs#209)///
[210](https://docs.rs#210)/// ```
[211](https://docs.rs#211)/// use divan::{Bencher, black_box};
[212](https://docs.rs#212)///
[213](https://docs.rs#213)/// #[divan::bench]
[214](https://docs.rs#214)/// fn copy_from_slice(bencher: Bencher) {
[215](https://docs.rs#215)///     let src = (0..100).collect::<Vec<i32>>();
[216](https://docs.rs#216)///     let mut dst = vec![0; src.len()];
[217](https://docs.rs#217)///
[218](https://docs.rs#218)///     bencher.bench_local(move || {
[219](https://docs.rs#219)///         black_box(&mut dst).copy_from_slice(black_box(&src));
[220](https://docs.rs#220)///     });
[221](https://docs.rs#221)/// }
[222](https://docs.rs#222)/// ```
[223](https://docs.rs#223)///
[224](https://docs.rs#224)/// Applying this attribute multiple times to the same item will cause a compile
[225](https://docs.rs#225)/// error:
[226](https://docs.rs#226)///
[227](https://docs.rs#227)/// ```compile_fail
[228](https://docs.rs#228)/// #[divan::bench]
[229](https://docs.rs#229)/// #[divan::bench]
[230](https://docs.rs#230)/// fn bench() {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)///     // ...
[232](https://docs.rs#232)/// }
[233](https://docs.rs#233)/// ```
[234](https://docs.rs#234)///
[235](https://docs.rs#235)/// # Drop
[236](https://docs.rs#236)///
[237](https://docs.rs#237)/// When a benchmarked function returns a value, it will not be [dropped][Drop]
[238](https://docs.rs#238)/// until after the current sample loop is finished. This allows for more
[239](https://docs.rs#239)/// precise timing measurements.
[240](https://docs.rs#240)///
[241](https://docs.rs#241)/// Note that there is an inherent memory cost to defer drop, including
[242](https://docs.rs#242)/// allocations inside not-yet-dropped values. Also, if the benchmark
[243](https://docs.rs#243)/// [panics](macro@std::panic), the values will never be dropped.
[244](https://docs.rs#244)///
[245](https://docs.rs#245)/// The following example benchmarks will only measure [`String`] construction
[246](https://docs.rs#246)/// time, but not deallocation time:
[247](https://docs.rs#247)///
[248](https://docs.rs#248)/// ```
[249](https://docs.rs#249)/// use divan::{Bencher, black_box};
[250](https://docs.rs#250)///
[251](https://docs.rs#251)/// #[divan::bench]
[252](https://docs.rs#252)/// fn freestanding() -> String {
[253](https://docs.rs#253)///     black_box("hello").to_uppercase()
[254](https://docs.rs#254)/// }
[255](https://docs.rs#255)///
[256](https://docs.rs#256)/// #[divan::bench]
[257](https://docs.rs#257)/// fn contextual(bencher: Bencher) {
[258](https://docs.rs#258)///     // Setup:
[259](https://docs.rs#259)///     let s: String = // ...
[260](https://docs.rs#260)///     # String::new();
[261](https://docs.rs#261)///
[262](https://docs.rs#262)///     bencher.bench(|| -> String {
[263](https://docs.rs#263)///         black_box(&s).to_lowercase()
[264](https://docs.rs#264)///     });
[265](https://docs.rs#265)/// }
[266](https://docs.rs#266)/// ```
[267](https://docs.rs#267)///
[268](https://docs.rs#268)/// If the returned value *does not* need to be dropped, there is no memory
[269](https://docs.rs#269)/// cost. Because of this, the following example benchmarks are equivalent:
[270](https://docs.rs#270)///
[271](https://docs.rs#271)/// ```
[272](https://docs.rs#272)/// #[divan::bench]
[273](https://docs.rs#273)/// fn with_return() -> i32 {
[274](https://docs.rs#274)///     let n: i32 = // ...
[275](https://docs.rs#275)///     # 0;
[276](https://docs.rs#276)///     n
[277](https://docs.rs#277)/// }
[278](https://docs.rs#278)///
[279](https://docs.rs#279)/// #[divan::bench]
[280](https://docs.rs#280)/// fn without_return() {
[281](https://docs.rs#281)///     let n: i32 = // ...
[282](https://docs.rs#282)///     # 0;
[283](https://docs.rs#283)///     divan::black_box(n);
[284](https://docs.rs#284)/// }
[285](https://docs.rs#285)/// ```
[286](https://docs.rs#286)///
[287](https://docs.rs#287)/// # Options

[306](https://docs.rs#306)/// ## `name`
[307](https://docs.rs#307)/// [`name`]: #name
[308](https://docs.rs#308)///
[309](https://docs.rs#309)/// By default, the benchmark uses the function's name. It can be overridden via
[310](https://docs.rs#310)/// the [`name`] option:
[311](https://docs.rs#311)///
[312](https://docs.rs#312)/// ```
[313](https://docs.rs#313)/// #[divan::bench(name = "my_add")]
[314](https://docs.rs#314)/// fn add() -> i32 {
[315](https://docs.rs#315)///     // Will appear as "crate_name::my_add".
[316](https://docs.rs#316)///     # 0
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// }
[318](https://docs.rs#318)/// ```
[319](https://docs.rs#319)///
[320](https://docs.rs#320)/// ## `crate`
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// [`crate`]: #crate
[322](https://docs.rs#322)///
[323](https://docs.rs#323)/// The path to the specific `divan` crate instance used by this macro's
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// generated code can be specified via the [`crate`] option. This is applicable
[325](https://docs.rs#325)/// when using `divan` via a macro from your own crate.
[326](https://docs.rs#326)///
[327](https://docs.rs#327)/// ```
[328](https://docs.rs#328)/// extern crate divan as sofa;
[329](https://docs.rs#329)///
[330](https://docs.rs#330)/// #[::sofa::bench(crate = ::sofa)]
[331](https://docs.rs#331)/// fn add() -> i32 {
[332](https://docs.rs#332)///     // ...
[333](https://docs.rs#333)///     # 0
[334](https://docs.rs#334)/// }
[335](https://docs.rs#335)/// ```
[336](https://docs.rs#336)///
[337](https://docs.rs#337)/// ## `args`
[338](https://docs.rs#338)/// [`args`]: #args
[339](https://docs.rs#339)///
[340](https://docs.rs#340)/// Function arguments can be provided to benchmark the function over multiple
[341](https://docs.rs#341)/// cases. This is used for comparing across parameters like collection lengths
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// and [`enum`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/keyword.enum.html) variants. If
[343](https://docs.rs#343)/// you are not comparing cases and just need to pass a value into the
[344](https://docs.rs#344)/// benchmark, instead consider passing local values into the [`Bencher::bench`]
[345](https://docs.rs#345)/// closure or use [`Bencher::with_inputs`] for many distinct values.
[346](https://docs.rs#346)///
[347](https://docs.rs#347)/// The following example benchmarks converting a [`Range`](std::ops::Range) to
[348](https://docs.rs#348)/// [`Vec`] over different lengths:
[349](https://docs.rs#349)///
[350](https://docs.rs#350)/// ```
[351](https://docs.rs#351)/// #[divan::bench(args = [1000, LEN, len()])]
[352](https://docs.rs#352)/// fn init_vec(len: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
[353](https://docs.rs#353)///     (0..len).collect()
[354](https://docs.rs#354)/// }
[355](https://docs.rs#355)///
[356](https://docs.rs#356)/// const LEN: usize = // ...
[357](https://docs.rs#357)/// # 0;
[358](https://docs.rs#358)///
[359](https://docs.rs#359)/// fn len() -> usize {
[360](https://docs.rs#360)///     // ...
[361](https://docs.rs#361)///     # 0
[362](https://docs.rs#362)/// }
[363](https://docs.rs#363)/// ```
[364](https://docs.rs#364)///
[365](https://docs.rs#365)/// The list of arguments can be shared across multiple benchmarks through an
[366](https://docs.rs#366)/// external [`Iterator`]:
[367](https://docs.rs#367)///
[368](https://docs.rs#368)/// ```
[369](https://docs.rs#369)/// const LENS: &[usize] = // ...
[370](https://docs.rs#370)/// # &[];
[371](https://docs.rs#371)///
[372](https://docs.rs#372)/// #[divan::bench(args = LENS)]
[373](https://docs.rs#373)/// fn bench_vec1(len: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
[374](https://docs.rs#374)///     // ...
[375](https://docs.rs#375)///     # vec![]
[376](https://docs.rs#376)/// }
[377](https://docs.rs#377)///
[378](https://docs.rs#378)/// #[divan::bench(args = LENS)]
[379](https://docs.rs#379)/// fn bench_vec2(len: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
[380](https://docs.rs#380)///     // ...
[381](https://docs.rs#381)///     # vec![]
[382](https://docs.rs#382)/// }
[383](https://docs.rs#383)/// ```
[384](https://docs.rs#384)///
[385](https://docs.rs#385)/// Unlike the [`consts`] option, any argument type is supported if it
[386](https://docs.rs#386)/// implements [`Any`], [`Copy`], [`Send`], [`Sync`], and [`ToString`] (or
[387](https://docs.rs#387)/// [`Debug`](std::fmt::Debug)):
[388](https://docs.rs#388)///
[389](https://docs.rs#389)/// ```
[390](https://docs.rs#390)/// #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
[391](https://docs.rs#391)/// enum Arg {
[392](https://docs.rs#392)///     A, B
[393](https://docs.rs#393)/// }
[394](https://docs.rs#394)///
[395](https://docs.rs#395)/// #[divan::bench(args = [Arg::A, Arg::B])]
[396](https://docs.rs#396)/// fn bench_args(arg: Arg) {
[397](https://docs.rs#397)///     // ...
[398](https://docs.rs#398)/// }
[399](https://docs.rs#399)/// ```
[400](https://docs.rs#400)///
[401](https://docs.rs#401)/// The argument type does not need to implement [`Copy`] if it is used through
[402](https://docs.rs#402)/// a reference:
[403](https://docs.rs#403)///
[404](https://docs.rs#404)/// ```
[405](https://docs.rs#405)/// #[derive(Debug)]
[406](https://docs.rs#406)/// enum Arg {
[407](https://docs.rs#407)///     A, B
[408](https://docs.rs#408)/// }
[409](https://docs.rs#409)///
[410](https://docs.rs#410)/// #[divan::bench(args = [Arg::A, Arg::B])]
[411](https://docs.rs#411)/// fn bench_args(arg: &Arg) {
[412](https://docs.rs#412)///     // ...
[413](https://docs.rs#413)/// }
[414](https://docs.rs#414)/// ```
[415](https://docs.rs#415)///
[416](https://docs.rs#416)/// For convenience, common string types are coerced to [`&str`](primitive@str):
[417](https://docs.rs#417)///
[418](https://docs.rs#418)/// ```
[419](https://docs.rs#419)/// fn strings() -> impl Iterator<Item = String> {
[420](https://docs.rs#420)///     // ...
[421](https://docs.rs#421)///     # [].into_iter()
[422](https://docs.rs#422)/// }
[423](https://docs.rs#423)///
[424](https://docs.rs#424)/// #[divan::bench(args = strings())]
[425](https://docs.rs#425)/// fn bench_strings(s: &str) {
[426](https://docs.rs#426)///     // ...
[427](https://docs.rs#427)/// }
[428](https://docs.rs#428)/// ```
[429](https://docs.rs#429)///
[430](https://docs.rs#430)/// Arguments can also be used with [`Bencher`]. This allows for generating
[431](https://docs.rs#431)/// inputs based on [`args`] values or providing throughput information via
[432](https://docs.rs#432)/// [`Counter`s](crate::counter::Counter):
[433](https://docs.rs#433)///
[434](https://docs.rs#434)/// ```
[435](https://docs.rs#435)/// # fn new_value<T>(v: T) -> T { v }
[436](https://docs.rs#436)/// # fn do_work<T>(_: T) {}
[437](https://docs.rs#437)/// use divan::Bencher;
[438](https://docs.rs#438)///
[439](https://docs.rs#439)/// #[divan::bench(args = [1, 2, 3])]
[440](https://docs.rs#440)/// fn bench(bencher: Bencher, len: usize) {
[441](https://docs.rs#441)///     let value = new_value(len);
[442](https://docs.rs#442)///
[443](https://docs.rs#443)///     bencher
[444](https://docs.rs#444)///         .counter(len)
[445](https://docs.rs#445)///         .bench(|| {
[446](https://docs.rs#446)///             do_work(value);
[447](https://docs.rs#447)///         });
[448](https://docs.rs#448)/// }
[449](https://docs.rs#449)/// ```
[450](https://docs.rs#450)///
[451](https://docs.rs#451)/// ## `consts`
[452](https://docs.rs#452)/// [`consts`]: #consts
[453](https://docs.rs#453)///
[454](https://docs.rs#454)/// Divan supports benchmarking functions with [`const`
[455](https://docs.rs#455)/// generics](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/generics.html#const-generics)
[456](https://docs.rs#456)/// via the [`consts`] option.
[457](https://docs.rs#457)///
[458](https://docs.rs#458)/// The following example benchmarks initialization of [`[i32; N]`](prim@array)
[459](https://docs.rs#459)/// for values of `N` provided by a [literal](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/literal-expr.html),
[460](https://docs.rs#460)/// [`const` item](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/constant-items.html),
[461](https://docs.rs#461)/// and [`const fn`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/const_eval.html#const-functions):
[462](https://docs.rs#462)///
[463](https://docs.rs#463)/// ```
[464](https://docs.rs#464)/// #[divan::bench(consts = [1000, LEN, len()])]
[465](https://docs.rs#465)/// fn init_array<const N: usize>() -> [i32; N] {
[466](https://docs.rs#466)///     let mut result = [0; N];
[467](https://docs.rs#467)///
[468](https://docs.rs#468)///     for i in 0..N {
[469](https://docs.rs#469)///         result[i] = divan::black_box(i as i32);
[470](https://docs.rs#470)///     }
[471](https://docs.rs#471)///
[472](https://docs.rs#472)///     result
[473](https://docs.rs#473)/// }
[474](https://docs.rs#474)///
[475](https://docs.rs#475)/// const LEN: usize = // ...
[476](https://docs.rs#476)/// # 0;
[477](https://docs.rs#477)///
[478](https://docs.rs#478)/// const fn len() -> usize {
[479](https://docs.rs#479)///     // ...
[480](https://docs.rs#480)///     # 0
[481](https://docs.rs#481)/// }
[482](https://docs.rs#482)/// ```
[483](https://docs.rs#483)///
[484](https://docs.rs#484)/// The list of constants can be shared across multiple benchmarks through an
[485](https://docs.rs#485)/// external [array](prim@array) or [slice](prim@slice):
[486](https://docs.rs#486)///
[487](https://docs.rs#487)/// ```
[488](https://docs.rs#488)/// const SIZES: &[usize] = &[1, 2, 5, 10];
[489](https://docs.rs#489)///
[490](https://docs.rs#490)/// #[divan::bench(consts = SIZES)]
[491](https://docs.rs#491)/// fn bench_array1<const N: usize>() -> [i32; N] {
[492](https://docs.rs#492)///     // ...
[493](https://docs.rs#493)///     # [0; N]
[494](https://docs.rs#494)/// }
[495](https://docs.rs#495)///
[496](https://docs.rs#496)/// #[divan::bench(consts = SIZES)]
[497](https://docs.rs#497)/// fn bench_array2<const N: usize>() -> [i32; N] {
[498](https://docs.rs#498)///     // ...
[499](https://docs.rs#499)///     # [0; N]
[500](https://docs.rs#500)/// }
[501](https://docs.rs#501)/// ```
[502](https://docs.rs#502)///
[503](https://docs.rs#503)/// External constants are limited to lengths 1 through 20, because of
[504](https://docs.rs#504)/// implementation details. This limit does not apply if the list is provided
[505](https://docs.rs#505)/// directly like in the first example.
[506](https://docs.rs#506)///
[507](https://docs.rs#507)/// ```compile_fail
[508](https://docs.rs#508)/// const SIZES: [usize; 21] = [
[509](https://docs.rs#509)///     // ...
[510](https://docs.rs#510)///     # 0; 21
[511](https://docs.rs#511)/// ];
[512](https://docs.rs#512)///
[513](https://docs.rs#513)/// #[divan::bench(consts = SIZES)]
[514](https://docs.rs#514)/// fn bench_array<const N: usize>() -> [i32; N] {
[515](https://docs.rs#515)///     // ...
[516](https://docs.rs#516)///     # [0; N]
[517](https://docs.rs#517)/// }
[518](https://docs.rs#518)/// ```
[519](https://docs.rs#519)///
[520](https://docs.rs#520)/// ## `types`
[521](https://docs.rs#521)/// [`types`]: #types
[522](https://docs.rs#522)///
[523](https://docs.rs#523)/// Divan supports benchmarking generic functions over a list of types via the
[524](https://docs.rs#524)/// [`types`] option.
[525](https://docs.rs#525)///
[526](https://docs.rs#526)/// The following example benchmarks the [`From<&str>`](From) implementations
[527](https://docs.rs#527)/// for [`&str`](prim@str) and [`String`]:
[528](https://docs.rs#528)///
[529](https://docs.rs#529)/// ```
[530](https://docs.rs#530)/// #[divan::bench(types = [&str, String])]
[531](https://docs.rs#531)/// fn from_str<'a, T>() -> T
[532](https://docs.rs#532)/// where
[533](https://docs.rs#533)///     T: From<&'a str>,
[534](https://docs.rs#534)/// {
[535](https://docs.rs#535)///     divan::black_box("hello world").into()
[536](https://docs.rs#536)/// }
[537](https://docs.rs#537)/// ```
[538](https://docs.rs#538)///
[539](https://docs.rs#539)/// The [`types`] and [`args`] options can be combined to benchmark _T_ × _A_
[540](https://docs.rs#540)/// scenarios. The following example benchmarks the [`FromIterator`]
[541](https://docs.rs#541)/// implementations for [`Vec`], [`BTreeSet`], and [`HashSet`]:
[542](https://docs.rs#542)///
[543](https://docs.rs#543)/// ```
[544](https://docs.rs#544)/// use std::collections::{BTreeSet, HashSet};
[545](https://docs.rs#545)///
[546](https://docs.rs#546)/// #[divan::bench(
[547](https://docs.rs#547)///     types = [Vec<i32>, BTreeSet<i32>, HashSet<i32>],
[548](https://docs.rs#548)///     args = [0, 2, 4, 16, 256, 4096],
[549](https://docs.rs#549)/// )]
[550](https://docs.rs#550)/// fn from_range<T>(n: i32) -> T
[551](https://docs.rs#551)/// where
[552](https://docs.rs#552)///     T: FromIterator<i32>,
[553](https://docs.rs#553)/// {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)///     (0..n).collect()
[555](https://docs.rs#555)/// }
[556](https://docs.rs#556)/// ```
[557](https://docs.rs#557)///
[558](https://docs.rs#558)/// [`BTreeSet`]: std::collections::BTreeSet
[559](https://docs.rs#559)/// [`HashSet`]: std::collections::HashSet
[560](https://docs.rs#560)///
[561](https://docs.rs#561)/// ## `sample_count`
[562](https://docs.rs#562)/// [`sample_count`]: #sample_count
[563](https://docs.rs#563)///
[564](https://docs.rs#564)/// The number of statistical sample recordings can be set to a predetermined
[565](https://docs.rs#565)/// [`u32`] value via the [`sample_count`] option. This may be overridden at
[566](https://docs.rs#566)/// runtime using either the `DIVAN_SAMPLE_COUNT` environment variable or
[567](https://docs.rs#567)/// `--sample-count` CLI argument.
[568](https://docs.rs#568)///
[569](https://docs.rs#569)/// ```
[570](https://docs.rs#570)/// #[divan::bench(sample_count = 1000)]
[571](https://docs.rs#571)/// fn add() -> i32 {
[572](https://docs.rs#572)///     // ...
[573](https://docs.rs#573)///     # 0
[574](https://docs.rs#574)/// }
[575](https://docs.rs#575)/// ```
[576](https://docs.rs#576)///
[577](https://docs.rs#577)/// If the [`threads`] option is enabled, sample count becomes a multiple of the
[578](https://docs.rs#578)/// number of threads. This is because each thread operates over the same sample
[579](https://docs.rs#579)/// size to ensure there are always N competing threads doing the same amount of
[580](https://docs.rs#580)/// work.
[581](https://docs.rs#581)///
[582](https://docs.rs#582)/// ## `sample_size`
[583](https://docs.rs#583)/// [`sample_size`]: #sample_size
[584](https://docs.rs#584)///
[585](https://docs.rs#585)/// The number iterations within each statistics sample can be set to a
[586](https://docs.rs#586)/// predetermined [`u32`] value via the [`sample_size`] option. This may be
[587](https://docs.rs#587)/// overridden at runtime using either the `DIVAN_SAMPLE_SIZE` environment
[588](https://docs.rs#588)/// variable or `--sample-size` CLI argument.
[589](https://docs.rs#589)///
[590](https://docs.rs#590)/// ```
[591](https://docs.rs#591)/// #[divan::bench(sample_size = 1000)]
[592](https://docs.rs#592)/// fn add() -> i32 {
[593](https://docs.rs#593)///     // ...
[594](https://docs.rs#594)///     # 0
[595](https://docs.rs#595)/// }
[596](https://docs.rs#596)/// ```
[597](https://docs.rs#597)///
[598](https://docs.rs#598)/// ## `threads`
[599](https://docs.rs#599)/// [`threads`]: #threads
[600](https://docs.rs#600)///
[601](https://docs.rs#601)/// Benchmarked functions can be run across multiple threads via the [`threads`]
[602](https://docs.rs#602)/// option. This enables you to measure contention on [atomics and
[603](https://docs.rs#603)/// locks][std::sync]. The default thread count is the [available parallelism].
[604](https://docs.rs#604)///
[605](https://docs.rs#605)/// ```
[606](https://docs.rs#606)/// use std::sync::Arc;
[607](https://docs.rs#607)///
[608](https://docs.rs#608)/// #[divan::bench(threads)]
[609](https://docs.rs#609)/// fn arc_clone(bencher: divan::Bencher) {
[610](https://docs.rs#610)///     let arc = Arc::new(42);
[611](https://docs.rs#611)///
[612](https://docs.rs#612)///     bencher.bench(|| arc.clone());
[613](https://docs.rs#613)/// }
[614](https://docs.rs#614)/// ```
[615](https://docs.rs#615)///
[616](https://docs.rs#616)/// The [`threads`] option can be set to any of:
[617](https://docs.rs#617)/// - [`bool`] for [available parallelism] (true) or no parallelism.
[618](https://docs.rs#618)/// - [`usize`] for a specific number of threads. 0 means use [available
[619](https://docs.rs#619)///   parallelism] and 1 means no parallelism.
[620](https://docs.rs#620)/// - [`IntoIterator`] over [`usize`] for multiple thread counts, such as:
[621](https://docs.rs#621)///     - [`Range<usize>`](std::ops::Range)
[622](https://docs.rs#622)///     - [`[usize; N]`](prim@array)
[623](https://docs.rs#623)///     - [`&[usize]`](prim@slice)
[624](https://docs.rs#624)///
[625](https://docs.rs#625)/// ```
[626](https://docs.rs#626)/// #[divan::bench(threads = false)]
[627](https://docs.rs#627)/// fn single() {
[628](https://docs.rs#628)///     // ...
[629](https://docs.rs#629)/// }
[630](https://docs.rs#630)///
[631](https://docs.rs#631)/// #[divan::bench(threads = 10)]
[632](https://docs.rs#632)/// fn specific() {
[633](https://docs.rs#633)///     // ...
[634](https://docs.rs#634)/// }
[635](https://docs.rs#635)///
[636](https://docs.rs#636)/// #[divan::bench(threads = 0..=8)]
[637](https://docs.rs#637)/// fn range() {
[638](https://docs.rs#638)///     // Note: Includes 0 for available parallelism.
[639](https://docs.rs#639)/// }
[640](https://docs.rs#640)///
[641](https://docs.rs#641)/// #[divan::bench(threads = [0, 1, 4, 8, 16])]
[642](https://docs.rs#642)/// fn selection() {
[643](https://docs.rs#643)///     // ...
[644](https://docs.rs#644)/// }
[645](https://docs.rs#645)/// ```
[646](https://docs.rs#646)///
[647](https://docs.rs#647)/// ## `counters`
[648](https://docs.rs#648)/// [`counters`]: #counters
[649](https://docs.rs#649)///
[650](https://docs.rs#650)/// The [`Counter`s](crate::counter::Counter) of each iteration can be set via
[651](https://docs.rs#651)/// the [`counters`] option. The following example emits info for the number of
[652](https://docs.rs#652)/// bytes and number of ints processed when benchmarking [slice sorting](slice::sort):
[653](https://docs.rs#653)///
[654](https://docs.rs#654)/// ```
[655](https://docs.rs#655)/// use divan::{Bencher, counter::{BytesCount, ItemsCount}};
[656](https://docs.rs#656)///
[657](https://docs.rs#657)/// const INTS: &[i32] = &[
[658](https://docs.rs#658)///     // ...
[659](https://docs.rs#659)/// ];
[660](https://docs.rs#660)///
[661](https://docs.rs#661)/// #[divan::bench(counters = [
[662](https://docs.rs#662)///     BytesCount::of_slice(INTS),
[663](https://docs.rs#663)///     ItemsCount::new(INTS.len()),
[664](https://docs.rs#664)/// ])]
[665](https://docs.rs#665)/// fn sort(bencher: Bencher) {
[666](https://docs.rs#666)///     bencher
[667](https://docs.rs#667)///         .with_inputs(|| INTS.to_vec())
[668](https://docs.rs#668)///         .bench_refs(|ints| ints.sort());
[669](https://docs.rs#669)/// }
[670](https://docs.rs#670)/// ```
[671](https://docs.rs#671)///
[672](https://docs.rs#672)/// For convenience, singular `counter` allows a single
[673](https://docs.rs#673)/// [`Counter`](crate::counter::Counter) to be set. The following example emits
[674](https://docs.rs#674)/// info for the number of bytes processed when benchmarking
[675](https://docs.rs#675)/// [`char`-counting](std::str::Chars::count):
[676](https://docs.rs#676)///
[677](https://docs.rs#677)/// ```
[678](https://docs.rs#678)/// use divan::counter::BytesCount;
[679](https://docs.rs#679)///
[680](https://docs.rs#680)/// const STR: &str = "...";
[681](https://docs.rs#681)///
[682](https://docs.rs#682)/// #[divan::bench(counter = BytesCount::of_str(STR))]
[683](https://docs.rs#683)/// fn char_count() -> usize {
[684](https://docs.rs#684)///     divan::black_box(STR).chars().count()
[685](https://docs.rs#685)/// }
[686](https://docs.rs#686)/// ```
[687](https://docs.rs#687)///
[688](https://docs.rs#688)/// See:
[689](https://docs.rs#689)/// - [`#[divan::bench_group(counters = ...)]`](macro@bench_group#counters)
[690](https://docs.rs#690)/// - [`Bencher::counter`]
[691](https://docs.rs#691)/// - [`Bencher::input_counter`]
[692](https://docs.rs#692)///
[693](https://docs.rs#693)/// ### `bytes_count`
[694](https://docs.rs#694)/// [`bytes_count`]: #bytes_count
[695](https://docs.rs#695)///
[696](https://docs.rs#696)/// Convenience shorthand for
[697](https://docs.rs#697)/// <code>[counter](#counters) = [BytesCount](counter::BytesCount)::from(n)</code>.
[698](https://docs.rs#698)///
[699](https://docs.rs#699)/// ### `chars_count`
[700](https://docs.rs#700)/// [`chars_count`]: #chars_count
[701](https://docs.rs#701)///
[702](https://docs.rs#702)/// Convenience shorthand for
[703](https://docs.rs#703)/// <code>[counter](#counters) = [CharsCount](counter::CharsCount)::from(n)</code>.
[704](https://docs.rs#704)///
[705](https://docs.rs#705)/// ### `items_count`
[706](https://docs.rs#706)/// [`items_count`]: #items_count
[707](https://docs.rs#707)///
[708](https://docs.rs#708)/// Convenience shorthand for
[709](https://docs.rs#709)/// <code>[counter](#counters) = [ItemsCount](counter::ItemsCount)::from(n)</code>.
[710](https://docs.rs#710)///
[711](https://docs.rs#711)/// ## `min_time`
[712](https://docs.rs#712)/// [`min_time`]: #min_time
[713](https://docs.rs#713)///
[714](https://docs.rs#714)/// The minimum time spent benchmarking each function can be set to a
[715](https://docs.rs#715)/// predetermined [`Duration`] via the [`min_time`] option. This may be
[716](https://docs.rs#716)/// overridden at runtime using either the `DIVAN_MIN_TIME` environment variable
[717](https://docs.rs#717)/// or `--min-time` CLI argument.
[718](https://docs.rs#718)///
[719](https://docs.rs#719)/// Unless [`skip_ext_time`] is set, this includes time external to the
[720](https://docs.rs#720)/// benchmarked function, such as time spent generating inputs and running
[721](https://docs.rs#721)/// [`Drop`].
[722](https://docs.rs#722)///
[723](https://docs.rs#723)/// ```
[724](https://docs.rs#724)/// use std::time::Duration;
[725](https://docs.rs#725)///
[726](https://docs.rs#726)/// #[divan::bench(min_time = Duration::from_secs(3))]
[727](https://docs.rs#727)/// fn add() -> i32 {
[728](https://docs.rs#728)///     // ...
[729](https://docs.rs#729)///     # 0
[730](https://docs.rs#730)/// }
[731](https://docs.rs#731)/// ```
[732](https://docs.rs#732)///
[733](https://docs.rs#733)/// For convenience, [`min_time`] can also be set with seconds as [`u64`] or
[734](https://docs.rs#734)/// [`f64`]. Invalid values will cause a panic at runtime.
[735](https://docs.rs#735)///
[736](https://docs.rs#736)/// ```
[737](https://docs.rs#737)/// #[divan::bench(min_time = 2)]
[738](https://docs.rs#738)/// fn int_secs() -> i32 {
[739](https://docs.rs#739)///     // ...
[740](https://docs.rs#740)///     # 0
[741](https://docs.rs#741)/// }
[742](https://docs.rs#742)///
[743](https://docs.rs#743)/// #[divan::bench(min_time = 1.5)]
[744](https://docs.rs#744)/// fn float_secs() -> i32 {
[745](https://docs.rs#745)///     // ...
[746](https://docs.rs#746)///     # 0
[747](https://docs.rs#747)/// }
[748](https://docs.rs#748)/// ```
[749](https://docs.rs#749)///
[750](https://docs.rs#750)/// ## `max_time`
[751](https://docs.rs#751)/// [`max_time`]: #max_time
[752](https://docs.rs#752)///
[753](https://docs.rs#753)/// The maximum time spent benchmarking each function can be set to a
[754](https://docs.rs#754)/// predetermined [`Duration`] via the [`max_time`] option. This may be
[755](https://docs.rs#755)/// overridden at runtime using either the `DIVAN_MAX_TIME` environment variable
[756](https://docs.rs#756)/// or `--max-time` CLI argument.
[757](https://docs.rs#757)///
[758](https://docs.rs#758)/// Unless [`skip_ext_time`] is set, this includes time external to the
[759](https://docs.rs#759)/// benchmarked function, such as time spent generating inputs and running
[760](https://docs.rs#760)/// [`Drop`].
[761](https://docs.rs#761)///
[762](https://docs.rs#762)/// If `min_time > max_time`, then [`max_time`] has priority and [`min_time`]
[763](https://docs.rs#763)/// will not be reached.
[764](https://docs.rs#764)///
[765](https://docs.rs#765)/// ```
[766](https://docs.rs#766)/// use std::time::Duration;
[767](https://docs.rs#767)///
[768](https://docs.rs#768)/// #[divan::bench(max_time = Duration::from_secs(5))]
[769](https://docs.rs#769)/// fn add() -> i32 {
[770](https://docs.rs#770)///     // ...
[771](https://docs.rs#771)///     # 0
[772](https://docs.rs#772)/// }
[773](https://docs.rs#773)/// ```
[774](https://docs.rs#774)///
[775](https://docs.rs#775)/// For convenience, like [`min_time`], [`max_time`] can also be set with
[776](https://docs.rs#776)/// seconds as [`u64`] or [`f64`]. Invalid values will cause a panic at runtime.
[777](https://docs.rs#777)///
[778](https://docs.rs#778)/// ```
[779](https://docs.rs#779)/// #[divan::bench(max_time = 8)]
[780](https://docs.rs#780)/// fn int_secs() -> i32 {
[781](https://docs.rs#781)///     // ...
[782](https://docs.rs#782)///     # 0
[783](https://docs.rs#783)/// }
[784](https://docs.rs#784)///
[785](https://docs.rs#785)/// #[divan::bench(max_time = 9.5)]
[786](https://docs.rs#786)/// fn float_secs() -> i32 {
[787](https://docs.rs#787)///     // ...
[788](https://docs.rs#788)///     # 0
[789](https://docs.rs#789)/// }
[790](https://docs.rs#790)/// ```
[791](https://docs.rs#791)///
[792](https://docs.rs#792)/// ## `skip_ext_time`
[793](https://docs.rs#793)/// [`skip_ext_time`]: #skip_ext_time
[794](https://docs.rs#794)///
[795](https://docs.rs#795)/// By default, [`min_time`] and [`max_time`] include time external to the
[796](https://docs.rs#796)/// benchmarked function, such as time spent generating inputs and running
[797](https://docs.rs#797)/// [`Drop`]. Enabling the [`skip_ext_time`] option will instead make those
[798](https://docs.rs#798)/// options only consider time spent within the benchmarked function. This may
[799](https://docs.rs#799)/// be overridden at runtime using either the `DIVAN_SKIP_EXT_TIME` environment
[800](https://docs.rs#800)/// variable or `--skip-ext-time` CLI argument.
[801](https://docs.rs#801)///
[802](https://docs.rs#802)/// In the following example, [`max_time`] only considers time spent running
[803](https://docs.rs#803)/// `measured_function`:
[804](https://docs.rs#804)///
[805](https://docs.rs#805)/// ```
[806](https://docs.rs#806)/// # fn generate_input() {}
[807](https://docs.rs#807)/// # fn measured_function(_: ()) {}
[808](https://docs.rs#808)/// #[divan::bench(max_time = 5, skip_ext_time)]
[809](https://docs.rs#809)/// fn bench(bencher: divan::Bencher) {
[810](https://docs.rs#810)///     bencher
[811](https://docs.rs#811)///         .with_inputs(|| generate_input())
[812](https://docs.rs#812)///         .bench_values(|input| measured_function(input));
[813](https://docs.rs#813)/// }
[814](https://docs.rs#814)/// ```
[815](https://docs.rs#815)///
[816](https://docs.rs#816)/// This option can be set to an explicit [`bool`] value to override parent
[817](https://docs.rs#817)/// values:
[818](https://docs.rs#818)///
[819](https://docs.rs#819)/// ```
[820](https://docs.rs#820)/// #[divan::bench(max_time = 5, skip_ext_time = false)]
[821](https://docs.rs#821)/// fn bench(bencher: divan::Bencher) {
[822](https://docs.rs#822)///     // ...
[823](https://docs.rs#823)/// }
[824](https://docs.rs#824)/// ```
[825](https://docs.rs#825)///
[826](https://docs.rs#826)/// ## `ignore`
[827](https://docs.rs#827)/// [`ignore`]: #ignore
[828](https://docs.rs#828)///
[829](https://docs.rs#829)/// Like [`#[test]`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/attributes/testing.html#the-test-attribute),
[830](https://docs.rs#830)/// `#[divan::bench]` functions can use [`#[ignore]`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/attributes/testing.html#the-ignore-attribute):
[831](https://docs.rs#831)///
[832](https://docs.rs#832)/// ```
[833](https://docs.rs#833)/// #[divan::bench]
[834](https://docs.rs#834)/// #[ignore]
[835](https://docs.rs#835)/// fn todo() {
[836](https://docs.rs#836)///     unimplemented!();
[837](https://docs.rs#837)/// }
[838](https://docs.rs#838)/// # divan::main();
[839](https://docs.rs#839)/// ```
[840](https://docs.rs#840)///
[841](https://docs.rs#841)/// This option can also instead be set within the `#[divan::bench]` attribute:
[842](https://docs.rs#842)///
[843](https://docs.rs#843)/// ```
[844](https://docs.rs#844)/// #[divan::bench(ignore)]
[845](https://docs.rs#845)/// fn todo() {
[846](https://docs.rs#846)///     unimplemented!();
[847](https://docs.rs#847)/// }
[848](https://docs.rs#848)/// # divan::main();
[849](https://docs.rs#849)/// ```
[850](https://docs.rs#850)///
[851](https://docs.rs#851)/// Like [`skip_ext_time`], this option can be set to an explicit [`bool`] value
[852](https://docs.rs#852)/// to override parent values:
[853](https://docs.rs#853)///
[854](https://docs.rs#854)/// ```
[855](https://docs.rs#855)/// #[divan::bench(ignore = false)]
[856](https://docs.rs#856)/// fn bench() {
[857](https://docs.rs#857)///     // ...
[858](https://docs.rs#858)/// }
[859](https://docs.rs#859)/// ```
[860](https://docs.rs#860)///
[861](https://docs.rs#861)/// This can be used to ignore benchmarks based on a runtime condition. The
[862](https://docs.rs#862)/// following example benchmark will be ignored if an [environment
[863](https://docs.rs#863)/// variable](std::env::var) is not set to "true":
[864](https://docs.rs#864)///
[865](https://docs.rs#865)/// ```
[866](https://docs.rs#866)/// #[divan::bench(
[867](https://docs.rs#867)///     ignore = std::env::var("BENCH_EXPENSIVE").as_deref() != Ok("true")
[868](https://docs.rs#868)/// )]
[869](https://docs.rs#869)/// fn expensive_bench() {
[870](https://docs.rs#870)///     // ...
[871](https://docs.rs#871)/// }
[872](https://docs.rs#872)/// ```
[873](https://docs.rs#873)///
[874](https://docs.rs#874)/// [`Any`]: std::any::Any
[875](https://docs.rs#875)/// [`Duration`]: std::time::Duration
[876](https://docs.rs#876)/// [available parallelism]: std::thread::available_parallelism
[877](https://docs.rs#877)pub use divan_macros::bench;
[878](https://docs.rs#878)
[879](https://docs.rs#879)/// Registers a benchmarking group.
[880](https://docs.rs#880)///
[881](https://docs.rs#881)/// # Examples
[882](https://docs.rs#882)///
[883](https://docs.rs#883)/// This is used for setting [options] shared across
[884](https://docs.rs#884)/// [`#[divan::bench]`](macro@bench) functions in the same module:
[885](https://docs.rs#885)///
[886](https://docs.rs#886)/// ```
[887](https://docs.rs#887)/// #[divan::bench_group(
[888](https://docs.rs#888)///     sample_count = 100,
[889](https://docs.rs#889)///     sample_size = 500,
[890](https://docs.rs#890)/// )]
[891](https://docs.rs#891)/// mod math {
[892](https://docs.rs#892)///     use divan::black_box;
[893](https://docs.rs#893)///
[894](https://docs.rs#894)///     #[divan::bench]
[895](https://docs.rs#895)///     fn add() -> i32 {
[896](https://docs.rs#896)///         black_box(1) + black_box(42)
[897](https://docs.rs#897)///     }
[898](https://docs.rs#898)///
[899](https://docs.rs#899)///     #[divan::bench]
[900](https://docs.rs#900)///     fn div() -> i32 {
[901](https://docs.rs#901)///         black_box(1) / black_box(42)
[902](https://docs.rs#902)///     }
[903](https://docs.rs#903)/// }
[904](https://docs.rs#904)///
[905](https://docs.rs#905)/// fn main() {
[906](https://docs.rs#906)///     // Run `math::add` and `math::div` benchmarks:
[907](https://docs.rs#907)///     divan::main();
[908](https://docs.rs#908)/// }
[909](https://docs.rs#909)/// ```
[910](https://docs.rs#910)///
[911](https://docs.rs#911)/// Benchmarking [options] set on parent groups cascade into child groups and
[912](https://docs.rs#912)/// their benchmarks:
[913](https://docs.rs#913)///
[914](https://docs.rs#914)/// ```
[915](https://docs.rs#915)/// #[divan::bench_group(
[916](https://docs.rs#916)///     sample_count = 100,
[917](https://docs.rs#917)///     sample_size = 500,
[918](https://docs.rs#918)/// )]
[919](https://docs.rs#919)/// mod parent {
[920](https://docs.rs#920)///     #[divan::bench_group(sample_size = 1)]
[921](https://docs.rs#921)///     mod child1 {
[922](https://docs.rs#922)///         #[divan::bench]
[923](https://docs.rs#923)///         fn bench() {
[924](https://docs.rs#924)///             // Will be sampled 100 times with 1 iteration per sample.
[925](https://docs.rs#925)///         }
[926](https://docs.rs#926)///     }
[927](https://docs.rs#927)///
[928](https://docs.rs#928)///     #[divan::bench_group(sample_count = 42)]
[929](https://docs.rs#929)///     mod child2 {
[930](https://docs.rs#930)///         #[divan::bench]
[931](https://docs.rs#931)///         fn bench() {
[932](https://docs.rs#932)///             // Will be sampled 42 times with 500 iterations per sample.
[933](https://docs.rs#933)///         }
[934](https://docs.rs#934)///     }
[935](https://docs.rs#935)///
[936](https://docs.rs#936)///     mod child3 {
[937](https://docs.rs#937)///         #[divan::bench(sample_count = 1)]
[938](https://docs.rs#938)///         fn bench() {
[939](https://docs.rs#939)///             // Will be sampled 1 time with 500 iterations per sample.
[940](https://docs.rs#940)///         }
[941](https://docs.rs#941)///     }
[942](https://docs.rs#942)/// }
[943](https://docs.rs#943)/// ```
[944](https://docs.rs#944)///
[945](https://docs.rs#945)/// Applying this attribute multiple times to the same item will cause a compile
[946](https://docs.rs#946)/// error:
[947](https://docs.rs#947)///
[948](https://docs.rs#948)/// ```compile_fail
[949](https://docs.rs#949)/// #[divan::bench_group]
[950](https://docs.rs#950)/// #[divan::bench_group]
[951](https://docs.rs#951)/// mod math {
[952](https://docs.rs#952)///     // ...
[953](https://docs.rs#953)/// }
[954](https://docs.rs#954)/// ```
[955](https://docs.rs#955)///
[956](https://docs.rs#956)/// # Options
[957](https://docs.rs#957)/// [options]: #options
[958](https://docs.rs#958)///
[959](https://docs.rs#959)/// - [`name`]
[960](https://docs.rs#960)/// - [`crate`]
[961](https://docs.rs#961)/// - [`sample_count`]
[962](https://docs.rs#962)/// - [`sample_size`]
[963](https://docs.rs#963)/// - [`threads`]
[964](https://docs.rs#964)/// - [`counters`]
[965](https://docs.rs#965)///     - [`bytes_count`]
[966](https://docs.rs#966)///     - [`chars_count`]
[967](https://docs.rs#967)///     - [`items_count`]
[968](https://docs.rs#968)/// - [`min_time`]
[969](https://docs.rs#969)/// - [`max_time`]
[970](https://docs.rs#970)/// - [`skip_ext_time`]
[971](https://docs.rs#971)/// - [`ignore`]
[972](https://docs.rs#972)///
[973](https://docs.rs#973)/// ## `name`
[974](https://docs.rs#974)/// [`name`]: #name
[975](https://docs.rs#975)///
[976](https://docs.rs#976)/// By default, the benchmark group uses the module's name. It can be overridden
[977](https://docs.rs#977)/// via the `name` option:
[978](https://docs.rs#978)///
[979](https://docs.rs#979)/// ```
[980](https://docs.rs#980)/// #[divan::bench_group(name = "my_math")]
[981](https://docs.rs#981)/// mod math {
[982](https://docs.rs#982)///     #[divan::bench(name = "my_add")]
[983](https://docs.rs#983)///     fn add() -> i32 {
[984](https://docs.rs#984)///         // Will appear as "crate_name::my_math::my_add".
[985](https://docs.rs#985)///         # 0
[986](https://docs.rs#986)///     }
[987](https://docs.rs#987)/// }
[988](https://docs.rs#988)/// ```
[989](https://docs.rs#989)///
[990](https://docs.rs#990)/// ## `crate`
[991](https://docs.rs#991)/// [`crate`]: #crate
[992](https://docs.rs#992)///
[993](https://docs.rs#993)/// The path to the specific `divan` crate instance used by this macro's
[994](https://docs.rs#994)/// generated code can be specified via the [`crate`] option. This is applicable
[995](https://docs.rs#995)/// when using `divan` via a macro from your own crate.
[996](https://docs.rs#996)///
[997](https://docs.rs#997)/// ```
[998](https://docs.rs#998)/// extern crate divan as sofa;
[999](https://docs.rs#999)///
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)/// #[::sofa::bench_group(crate = ::sofa)]
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)/// mod math {
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)///     #[::sofa::bench(crate = ::sofa)]
[1003](https://docs.rs#1003)///     fn add() -> i32 {
[1004](https://docs.rs#1004)///         // ...
[1005](https://docs.rs#1005)///         # 0
[1006](https://docs.rs#1006)///     }
[1007](https://docs.rs#1007)/// }
[1008](https://docs.rs#1008)/// ```
[1009](https://docs.rs#1009)///
[1010](https://docs.rs#1010)/// ## `sample_count`
[1011](https://docs.rs#1011)/// [`sample_count`]: #sample_count
[1012](https://docs.rs#1012)///
[1013](https://docs.rs#1013)/// The number of statistical sample recordings can be set to a predetermined
[1014](https://docs.rs#1014)/// [`u32`] value via the [`sample_count`] option. This may be overridden at
[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)/// runtime using either the `DIVAN_SAMPLE_COUNT` environment variable or
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)/// `--sample-count` CLI argument.
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)///
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)/// ```
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)/// #[divan::bench_group(sample_count = 1000)]
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)/// mod math {
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)///     #[divan::bench]
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022)///     fn add() -> i32 {
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)///         // ...
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)///         # 0
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)///     }
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)/// }
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)/// ```
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)///
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)/// If the [`threads`] option is enabled, sample count becomes a multiple of the
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)/// number of threads. This is because each thread operates over the same sample
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)/// size to ensure there are always N competing threads doing the same amount of
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)/// work.
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)///
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)/// ## `sample_size`
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)/// [`sample_size`]: #sample_size
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)///
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)/// The number iterations within each statistical sample can be set to a
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)/// predetermined [`u32`] value via the [`sample_size`] option. This may be
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)/// overridden at runtime using either the `DIVAN_SAMPLE_SIZE` environment
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)/// variable or `--sample-size` CLI argument.
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)///
[1042](https://docs.rs#1042)/// ```
[1043](https://docs.rs#1043)/// #[divan::bench_group(sample_size = 1000)]
[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)/// mod math {
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)///     #[divan::bench]
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)///     fn add() -> i32 {
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)///         // ...
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)///         # 0
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)///     }
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)/// }
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)/// ```
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)///
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)/// ## `threads`
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)/// [`threads`]: #threads
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)///
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)/// See [`#[divan::bench(threads = ...)]`](macro@bench#threads).
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)///
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)/// ## `counters`
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)/// [`counters`]: #counters
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)///
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)/// The [`Counter`s](crate::counter::Counter) of each iteration of benchmarked
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)/// functions in a group can be set via the [`counters`] option. The following
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)/// example emits info for the number of bytes and number of ints processed when
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)/// benchmarking [slice sorting](slice::sort):
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)///
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)/// ```
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)/// use divan::{Bencher, counter::{BytesCount, ItemsCount}};
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)///
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)/// const INTS: &[i32] = &[
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)///     // ...
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)/// ];
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)///
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)/// #[divan::bench_group(counters = [
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)///     BytesCount::of_slice(INTS),
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)///     ItemsCount::new(INTS.len()),
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)/// ])]
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)/// mod sort {
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)///     use super::*;
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)///
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)///     #[divan::bench]
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)///     fn default(bencher: Bencher) {
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)///         bencher
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)///             .with_inputs(|| INTS.to_vec())
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)///             .bench_refs(|ints| ints.sort());
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)///     }
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)///
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)///     #[divan::bench]
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)///     fn unstable(bencher: Bencher) {
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)///         bencher
[1090](https://docs.rs#1090)///             .with_inputs(|| INTS.to_vec())
[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)///             .bench_refs(|ints| ints.sort_unstable());
[1092](https://docs.rs#1092)///     }
[1093](https://docs.rs#1093)/// }
[1094](https://docs.rs#1094)/// # fn main() {}
[1095](https://docs.rs#1095)/// ```
[1096](https://docs.rs#1096)///
[1097](https://docs.rs#1097)/// For convenience, singular `counter` allows a single
[1098](https://docs.rs#1098)/// [`Counter`](crate::counter::Counter) to be set. The following example emits
[1099](https://docs.rs#1099)/// info for the number of bytes processed when benchmarking
[1100](https://docs.rs#1100)/// [`char`-counting](std::str::Chars::count) and
[1101](https://docs.rs#1101)/// [`char`-collecting](std::str::Chars::collect):
[1102](https://docs.rs#1102)///
[1103](https://docs.rs#1103)/// ```
[1104](https://docs.rs#1104)/// use divan::counter::BytesCount;
[1105](https://docs.rs#1105)///
[1106](https://docs.rs#1106)/// const STR: &str = "...";
[1107](https://docs.rs#1107)///
[1108](https://docs.rs#1108)/// #[divan::bench_group(counter = BytesCount::of_str(STR))]
[1109](https://docs.rs#1109)/// mod chars {
[1110](https://docs.rs#1110)///     use super::STR;
[1111](https://docs.rs#1111)///
[1112](https://docs.rs#1112)///     #[divan::bench]
[1113](https://docs.rs#1113)///     fn count() -> usize {
[1114](https://docs.rs#1114)///         divan::black_box(STR).chars().count()
[1115](https://docs.rs#1115)///     }
[1116](https://docs.rs#1116)///
[1117](https://docs.rs#1117)///     #[divan::bench]
[1118](https://docs.rs#1118)///     fn collect() -> String {
[1119](https://docs.rs#1119)///         divan::black_box(STR).chars().collect()
[1120](https://docs.rs#1120)///     }
[1121](https://docs.rs#1121)/// }
[1122](https://docs.rs#1122)/// # fn main() {}
[1123](https://docs.rs#1123)/// ```
[1124](https://docs.rs#1124)///
[1125](https://docs.rs#1125)/// See:
[1126](https://docs.rs#1126)/// - [`#[divan::bench(counters = ...)]`](macro@bench#counters)
[1127](https://docs.rs#1127)/// - [`Bencher::counter`]
[1128](https://docs.rs#1128)/// - [`Bencher::input_counter`]
[1129](https://docs.rs#1129)///
[1130](https://docs.rs#1130)/// ### `bytes_count`

[1154](https://docs.rs#1154)/// ## `min_time`
[1155](https://docs.rs#1155)/// [`min_time`]: #min_time
[1156](https://docs.rs#1156)///
[1157](https://docs.rs#1157)/// The minimum time spent benchmarking each function can be set to a
[1158](https://docs.rs#1158)/// predetermined [`Duration`] via the [`min_time`] option. This may be
[1159](https://docs.rs#1159)/// overridden at runtime using either the `DIVAN_MIN_TIME` environment variable
[1160](https://docs.rs#1160)/// or `--min-time` CLI argument.
[1161](https://docs.rs#1161)///
[1162](https://docs.rs#1162)/// Unless [`skip_ext_time`] is set, this includes time external to benchmarked
[1163](https://docs.rs#1163)/// functions, such as time spent generating inputs and running [`Drop`].
[1164](https://docs.rs#1164)///
[1165](https://docs.rs#1165)/// ```
[1166](https://docs.rs#1166)/// use std::time::Duration;
[1167](https://docs.rs#1167)///
[1168](https://docs.rs#1168)/// #[divan::bench_group(min_time = Duration::from_secs(3))]
[1169](https://docs.rs#1169)/// mod math {
[1170](https://docs.rs#1170)///     #[divan::bench]
[1171](https://docs.rs#1171)///     fn add() -> i32 {
[1172](https://docs.rs#1172)///         // ...
[1173](https://docs.rs#1173)///         # 0
[1174](https://docs.rs#1174)///     }
[1175](https://docs.rs#1175)/// }
[1176](https://docs.rs#1176)/// ```
[1177](https://docs.rs#1177)///
[1178](https://docs.rs#1178)/// For convenience, [`min_time`] can also be set with seconds as [`u64`] or
[1179](https://docs.rs#1179)/// [`f64`]. Invalid values will cause a panic at runtime.
[1180](https://docs.rs#1180)///
[1181](https://docs.rs#1181)/// ```
[1182](https://docs.rs#1182)/// #[divan::bench_group(min_time = 2)]
[1183](https://docs.rs#1183)/// mod int_secs {
[1184](https://docs.rs#1184)///     // ...
[1185](https://docs.rs#1185)/// }
[1186](https://docs.rs#1186)///
[1187](https://docs.rs#1187)/// #[divan::bench_group(min_time = 1.5)]
[1188](https://docs.rs#1188)/// mod float_secs {
[1189](https://docs.rs#1189)///     // ...
[1190](https://docs.rs#1190)/// }
[1191](https://docs.rs#1191)/// ```
[1192](https://docs.rs#1192)///
[1193](https://docs.rs#1193)/// ## `max_time`
[1194](https://docs.rs#1194)/// [`max_time`]: #max_time
[1195](https://docs.rs#1195)///
[1196](https://docs.rs#1196)/// The maximum time spent benchmarking each function can be set to a
[1197](https://docs.rs#1197)/// predetermined [`Duration`] via the [`max_time`] option. This may be
[1198](https://docs.rs#1198)/// overridden at runtime using either the `DIVAN_MAX_TIME` environment variable
[1199](https://docs.rs#1199)/// or `--max-time` CLI argument.
[1200](https://docs.rs#1200)///
[1201](https://docs.rs#1201)/// Unless [`skip_ext_time`] is set, this includes time external to benchmarked
[1202](https://docs.rs#1202)/// functions, such as time spent generating inputs and running [`Drop`].
[1203](https://docs.rs#1203)///
[1204](https://docs.rs#1204)/// If `min_time > max_time`, then [`max_time`] has priority and [`min_time`]
[1205](https://docs.rs#1205)/// will not be reached.
[1206](https://docs.rs#1206)///
[1207](https://docs.rs#1207)/// ```
[1208](https://docs.rs#1208)/// use std::time::Duration;
[1209](https://docs.rs#1209)///
[1210](https://docs.rs#1210)/// #[divan::bench_group(max_time = Duration::from_secs(5))]
[1211](https://docs.rs#1211)/// mod math {
[1212](https://docs.rs#1212)///     #[divan::bench]
[1213](https://docs.rs#1213)///     fn add() -> i32 {
[1214](https://docs.rs#1214)///         // ...
[1215](https://docs.rs#1215)///         # 0
[1216](https://docs.rs#1216)///     }
[1217](https://docs.rs#1217)/// }
[1218](https://docs.rs#1218)/// ```
[1219](https://docs.rs#1219)///
[1220](https://docs.rs#1220)/// For convenience, like [`min_time`], [`max_time`] can also be set with
[1221](https://docs.rs#1221)/// seconds as [`u64`] or [`f64`]. Invalid values will cause a panic at runtime.
[1222](https://docs.rs#1222)///
[1223](https://docs.rs#1223)/// ```
[1224](https://docs.rs#1224)/// #[divan::bench_group(max_time = 8)]
[1225](https://docs.rs#1225)/// mod int_secs {
[1226](https://docs.rs#1226)///     // ...
[1227](https://docs.rs#1227)/// }
[1228](https://docs.rs#1228)///
[1229](https://docs.rs#1229)/// #[divan::bench_group(max_time = 9.5)]
[1230](https://docs.rs#1230)/// mod float_secs {
[1231](https://docs.rs#1231)///     // ...
[1232](https://docs.rs#1232)/// }
[1233](https://docs.rs#1233)/// ```
[1234](https://docs.rs#1234)///
[1235](https://docs.rs#1235)/// ## `skip_ext_time`
[1236](https://docs.rs#1236)/// [`skip_ext_time`]: #skip_ext_time
[1237](https://docs.rs#1237)///
[1238](https://docs.rs#1238)/// By default, [`min_time`] and [`max_time`] include time external to
[1239](https://docs.rs#1239)/// benchmarked functions, such as time spent generating inputs and running
[1240](https://docs.rs#1240)/// [`Drop`]. Enabling the [`skip_ext_time`] option will instead make those
[1241](https://docs.rs#1241)/// options only consider time spent within benchmarked functions. This may be
[1242](https://docs.rs#1242)/// overridden at runtime using either the `DIVAN_SKIP_EXT_TIME` environment
[1243](https://docs.rs#1243)/// variable or `--skip-ext-time` CLI argument.
[1244](https://docs.rs#1244)///
[1245](https://docs.rs#1245)/// In the following example, [`max_time`] only considers time spent running
[1246](https://docs.rs#1246)/// `measured_function`:
[1247](https://docs.rs#1247)///
[1248](https://docs.rs#1248)/// ```
[1249](https://docs.rs#1249)/// #[divan::bench_group(skip_ext_time)]
[1250](https://docs.rs#1250)/// mod group {
[1251](https://docs.rs#1251)///     # fn generate_input() {}
[1252](https://docs.rs#1252)///     # fn measured_function(_: ()) {}
[1253](https://docs.rs#1253)///     #[divan::bench(max_time = 5)]
[1254](https://docs.rs#1254)///     fn bench(bencher: divan::Bencher) {
[1255](https://docs.rs#1255)///         bencher
[1256](https://docs.rs#1256)///             .with_inputs(|| generate_input())
[1257](https://docs.rs#1257)///             .bench_values(|input| measured_function(input));
[1258](https://docs.rs#1258)///     }
[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)/// }
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)/// ```
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)///
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)/// This option can be set to an explicit [`bool`] value to override parent
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)/// values:
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)///
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)/// ```
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)/// #[divan::bench_group(skip_ext_time = false)]
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)/// mod group {
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)///     // ...
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)/// }
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)/// ```
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)///
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)/// ## `ignore`
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)/// [`ignore`]: #ignore
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)///
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)/// Like [`#[test]`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/attributes/testing.html#the-test-attribute)
[1276](https://docs.rs#1276)/// and [`#[divan::bench]`](macro@bench), `#[divan::bench_group]` functions can
[1277](https://docs.rs#1277)/// use [`#[ignore]`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/attributes/testing.html#the-ignore-attribute):
[1278](https://docs.rs#1278)///
[1279](https://docs.rs#1279)/// ```
[1280](https://docs.rs#1280)/// #[divan::bench_group]
[1281](https://docs.rs#1281)/// #[ignore]
[1282](https://docs.rs#1282)/// mod math {
[1283](https://docs.rs#1283)///     #[divan::bench]
[1284](https://docs.rs#1284)///     fn todo() {
[1285](https://docs.rs#1285)///         unimplemented!();
[1286](https://docs.rs#1286)///     }
[1287](https://docs.rs#1287)/// }
[1288](https://docs.rs#1288)/// # divan::main();
[1289](https://docs.rs#1289)/// ```
[1290](https://docs.rs#1290)///
[1291](https://docs.rs#1291)/// This option can also instead be set within the `#[divan::bench_group]`
[1292](https://docs.rs#1292)/// attribute:
[1293](https://docs.rs#1293)///
[1294](https://docs.rs#1294)/// ```
[1295](https://docs.rs#1295)/// #[divan::bench_group(ignore)]
[1296](https://docs.rs#1296)/// mod math {
[1297](https://docs.rs#1297)///     #[divan::bench]
[1298](https://docs.rs#1298)///     fn todo() {
[1299](https://docs.rs#1299)///         unimplemented!();
[1300](https://docs.rs#1300)///     }
[1301](https://docs.rs#1301)/// }
[1302](https://docs.rs#1302)/// # divan::main();
[1303](https://docs.rs#1303)/// ```
[1304](https://docs.rs#1304)///
[1305](https://docs.rs#1305)/// Like [`skip_ext_time`], this option can be set to an explicit [`bool`] value
[1306](https://docs.rs#1306)/// to override parent values:
[1307](https://docs.rs#1307)///
[1308](https://docs.rs#1308)/// ```
[1309](https://docs.rs#1309)/// #[divan::bench_group(ignore = false)]
[1310](https://docs.rs#1310)/// mod group {
[1311](https://docs.rs#1311)///     // ...
[1312](https://docs.rs#1312)/// }
[1313](https://docs.rs#1313)/// ```
[1314](https://docs.rs#1314)///
[1315](https://docs.rs#1315)/// This can be used to ignore benchmarks based on a runtime condition. The
[1316](https://docs.rs#1316)/// following example benchmark group will be ignored if an [environment
[1317](https://docs.rs#1317)/// variable](std::env::var) is not set to "true":
[1318](https://docs.rs#1318)///
[1319](https://docs.rs#1319)/// ```
[1320](https://docs.rs#1320)/// #[divan::bench_group(
[1321](https://docs.rs#1321)///     ignore = std::env::var("BENCH_EXPENSIVE").as_deref() != Ok("true")
[1322](https://docs.rs#1322)/// )]
[1323](https://docs.rs#1323)/// mod expensive_benches {
[1324](https://docs.rs#1324)///     // ...
[1325](https://docs.rs#1325)/// }
[1326](https://docs.rs#1326)/// ```
[1327](https://docs.rs#1327)///
[1328](https://docs.rs#1328)/// [`Duration`]: std::time::Duration
[1329](https://docs.rs#1329)pub use divan_macros::bench_group;

# bench in divan - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/divan/0.1.21/divan/attr.bench.html

`#[bench]`## Expand description

Registers a benchmarking function.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

The quickest way to get started is to benchmark the function as-is:

```
use divan::black_box;
#[divan::bench]
fn add() -> i32 {
    black_box(1) + black_box(42)
}
fn main() {
    // Run `add` benchmark:
    divan::main();
}
```
If benchmarks need to setup context before running, they can take a
[ Bencher](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html) and use

[:](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html#method.bench)

`Bencher::bench````
use divan::{Bencher, black_box};
#[divan::bench]
fn copy_from_slice(bencher: Bencher) {
    let src = (0..100).collect::<Vec<i32>>();
    let mut dst = vec![0; src.len()];
    bencher.bench_local(move || {
        black_box(&mut dst).copy_from_slice(black_box(&src));
    });
}
```
Applying this attribute multiple times to the same item will cause a compile error:

[§](https://docs.rs#drop)Drop

When a benchmarked function returns a value, it will not be [dropped](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html)
until after the current sample loop is finished. This allows for more
precise timing measurements.

Note that there is an inherent memory cost to defer drop, including
allocations inside not-yet-dropped values. Also, if the benchmark
[panics](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/macro.panic.html), the values will never be dropped.

The following example benchmarks will only measure [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html) construction
time, but not deallocation time:

```
use divan::{Bencher, black_box};
#[divan::bench]
fn freestanding() -> String {
    black_box("hello").to_uppercase()
}
#[divan::bench]
fn contextual(bencher: Bencher) {
    // Setup:
    let s: String = // ...
    bencher.bench(|| -> String {
        black_box(&s).to_lowercase()
    });
}
```
If the returned value *does not* need to be dropped, there is no memory
cost. Because of this, the following example benchmarks are equivalent:

```
#[divan::bench]
fn with_return() -> i32 {
    let n: i32 = // ...
    n
}
#[divan::bench]
fn without_return() {
    let n: i32 = // ...
    divan::black_box(n);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#options)Options

- `name`
- `crate`
- `args`
- `consts`
- `types`
- `sample_count`
- `sample_size`
- `threads`
- `counters`
- `min_time`
- `max_time`
- `skip_ext_time`
- `ignore`

[§](https://docs.rs#name)`name`

By default, the benchmark uses the function’s name. It can be overridden via
the [ name](https://docs.rs#name) option:

```
#[divan::bench(name = "my_add")]
fn add() -> i32 {
    // Will appear as "crate_name::my_add".
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#crate)`crate`

The path to the specific `divan` crate instance used by this macro’s
generated code can be specified via the [ crate](https://docs.rs#crate) option. This is applicable
when using

`divan` via a macro from your own crate.```
extern crate divan as sofa;
#[::sofa::bench(crate = ::sofa)]
fn add() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#args)`args`

Function arguments can be provided to benchmark the function over multiple
cases. This is used for comparing across parameters like collection lengths
and [ enum](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/keyword.enum.html) variants. If
you are not comparing cases and just need to pass a value into the
benchmark, instead consider passing local values into the

[closure or use](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html#method.bench)

`Bencher::bench`[for many distinct values.](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html#method.with_inputs)

`Bencher::with_inputs`The following example benchmarks converting a [ Range](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/range/struct.Range.html) to

[over different lengths:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)

`Vec````
#[divan::bench(args = [1000, LEN, len()])]
fn init_vec(len: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
    (0..len).collect()
}
const LEN: usize = // ...
fn len() -> usize {
    // ...
}
```
The list of arguments can be shared across multiple benchmarks through an
external [ Iterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/iterator/trait.Iterator.html):

```
const LENS: &[usize] = // ...
#[divan::bench(args = LENS)]
fn bench_vec1(len: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
    // ...
}
#[divan::bench(args = LENS)]
fn bench_vec2(len: usize) -> Vec<usize> {
    // ...
}
```
Unlike the [ consts](https://docs.rs#consts) option, any argument type is supported if it
implements

[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/any/trait.Any.html)

`Any`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html)

`Copy`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Send.html)

`Send`[, and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sync.html)

`Sync`[(or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/trait.ToString.html)

`ToString`[):](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html)

`Debug````
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]
enum Arg {
    A, B
}
#[divan::bench(args = [Arg::A, Arg::B])]
fn bench_args(arg: Arg) {
    // ...
}
```
The argument type does not need to implement [ Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Copy.html) if it is used through
a reference:

```
#[derive(Debug)]
enum Arg {
    A, B
}
#[divan::bench(args = [Arg::A, Arg::B])]
fn bench_args(arg: &Arg) {
    // ...
}
```
For convenience, common string types are coerced to [ &str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html):

```
fn strings() -> impl Iterator<Item = String> {
    // ...
}
#[divan::bench(args = strings())]
fn bench_strings(s: &str) {
    // ...
}
```
Arguments can also be used with [ Bencher](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html). This allows for generating
inputs based on

[values or providing throughput information via](https://docs.rs#args)

`args`[:](https://docs.rs/counter/trait.Counter.html)

`Counter`s```
use divan::Bencher;
#[divan::bench(args = [1, 2, 3])]
fn bench(bencher: Bencher, len: usize) {
    let value = new_value(len);
    bencher
        .counter(len)
        .bench(|| {
            do_work(value);
        });
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#consts)`consts`

Divan supports benchmarking functions with [ const
generics](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/generics.html#const-generics)
via the

[option.](https://docs.rs#consts)

`consts`The following example benchmarks initialization of [ [i32; N]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html)
for values of

`N` provided by a [literal](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/expressions/literal-expr.html),

[, and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/constant-items.html)

`const` item[:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/const_eval.html#const-functions)

`const fn````
#[divan::bench(consts = [1000, LEN, len()])]
fn init_array<const N: usize>() -> [i32; N] {
    let mut result = [0; N];
    for i in 0..N {
        result[i] = divan::black_box(i as i32);
    }
    result
}
const LEN: usize = // ...
const fn len() -> usize {
    // ...
}
```
The list of constants can be shared across multiple benchmarks through an
external [array](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.array.html) or [slice](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html):

```
const SIZES: &[usize] = &[1, 2, 5, 10];
#[divan::bench(consts = SIZES)]
fn bench_array1<const N: usize>() -> [i32; N] {
    // ...
}
#[divan::bench(consts = SIZES)]
fn bench_array2<const N: usize>() -> [i32; N] {
    // ...
}
```
External constants are limited to lengths 1 through 20, because of implementation details. This limit does not apply if the list is provided directly like in the first example.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
const SIZES: [usize; 21] = [
    // ...
];
#[divan::bench(consts = SIZES)]
fn bench_array<const N: usize>() -> [i32; N] {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#types)`types`

Divan supports benchmarking generic functions over a list of types via the
[ types](https://docs.rs#types) option.

The following example benchmarks the [ From<&str>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html) implementations
for

[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)

`&str`[:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`String````
#[divan::bench(types = [&str, String])]
fn from_str<'a, T>() -> T
where
    T: From<&'a str>,
{
    divan::black_box("hello world").into()
}
```
The [ types](https://docs.rs#types) and

[options can be combined to benchmark](https://docs.rs#args)

`args`*T*×

*A*scenarios. The following example benchmarks the

[implementations for](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.FromIterator.html)

`FromIterator`[,](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)

`Vec`[, and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/set/struct.BTreeSet.html)

`BTreeSet`[:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/collections/hash/set/struct.HashSet.html)

`HashSet````
use std::collections::{BTreeSet, HashSet};
#[divan::bench(
    types = [Vec<i32>, BTreeSet<i32>, HashSet<i32>],
    args = [0, 2, 4, 16, 256, 4096],
)]
fn from_range<T>(n: i32) -> T
where
    T: FromIterator<i32>,
{
    (0..n).collect()
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#sample_count)`sample_count`

The number of statistical sample recordings can be set to a predetermined
[ u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) value via the

[option. This may be overridden at runtime using either the](https://docs.rs#sample_count)

`sample_count``DIVAN_SAMPLE_COUNT` environment variable or
`--sample-count` CLI argument.```
#[divan::bench(sample_count = 1000)]
fn add() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
```
If the [ threads](https://docs.rs#threads) option is enabled, sample count becomes a multiple of the
number of threads. This is because each thread operates over the same sample
size to ensure there are always N competing threads doing the same amount of
work.

[§](https://docs.rs#sample_size)`sample_size`

The number iterations within each statistics sample can be set to a
predetermined [ u32](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u32.html) value via the

[option. This may be overridden at runtime using either the](https://docs.rs#sample_size)

`sample_size``DIVAN_SAMPLE_SIZE` environment
variable or `--sample-size` CLI argument.```
#[divan::bench(sample_size = 1000)]
fn add() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#threads)`threads`

Benchmarked functions can be run across multiple threads via the [ threads](https://docs.rs#threads)
option. This enables you to measure contention on

[atomics and locks](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/sync/index.html). The default thread count is the

[available parallelism](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/thread/functions/fn.available_parallelism.html).

```
use std::sync::Arc;
#[divan::bench(threads)]
fn arc_clone(bencher: divan::Bencher) {
    let arc = Arc::new(42);
    bencher.bench(|| arc.clone());
}
```
The [ threads](https://docs.rs#threads) option can be set to any of:

- `bool`- [available parallelism](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/thread/functions/fn.available_parallelism.html)(true) or no parallelism.
- `usize`- [available parallelism](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/thread/functions/fn.available_parallelism.html)and 1 means no parallelism.
- `IntoIterator`- `usize`

```
#[divan::bench(threads = false)]
fn single() {
    // ...
}
#[divan::bench(threads = 10)]
fn specific() {
    // ...
}
#[divan::bench(threads = 0..=8)]
fn range() {
    // Note: Includes 0 for available parallelism.
}
#[divan::bench(threads = [0, 1, 4, 8, 16])]
fn selection() {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#counters)`counters`

The [ Counters](https://docs.rs/counter/trait.Counter.html) of each iteration can be set via
the

[option. The following example emits info for the number of bytes and number of ints processed when benchmarking](https://docs.rs#counters)

`counters`[slice sorting](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html#method.sort):

```
use divan::{Bencher, counter::{BytesCount, ItemsCount}};
const INTS: &[i32] = &[
    // ...
];
#[divan::bench(counters = [
    BytesCount::of_slice(INTS),
    ItemsCount::new(INTS.len()),
])]
fn sort(bencher: Bencher) {
    bencher
        .with_inputs(|| INTS.to_vec())
        .bench_refs(|ints| ints.sort());
}
```
For convenience, singular `counter` allows a single
[ Counter](https://docs.rs/counter/trait.Counter.html) to be set. The following example emits
info for the number of bytes processed when benchmarking

[:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/str/iter/struct.Chars.html#method.count)

`char`-counting```
use divan::counter::BytesCount;
const STR: &str = "...";
#[divan::bench(counter = BytesCount::of_str(STR))]
fn char_count() -> usize {
    divan::black_box(STR).chars().count()
}
```
See:

[§](https://docs.rs#bytes_count)`bytes_count`

Convenience shorthand for
[counter](https://docs.rs#counters) = [BytesCount](https://docs.rs/counter/struct.BytesCount.html)::from(n)

[§](https://docs.rs#chars_count)`chars_count`

Convenience shorthand for
[counter](https://docs.rs#counters) = [CharsCount](https://docs.rs/counter/struct.CharsCount.html)::from(n)

[§](https://docs.rs#items_count)`items_count`

Convenience shorthand for
[counter](https://docs.rs#counters) = [ItemsCount](https://docs.rs/counter/struct.ItemsCount.html)::from(n)

[§](https://docs.rs#min_time)`min_time`

The minimum time spent benchmarking each function can be set to a
predetermined [ Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html) via the

[option. This may be overridden at runtime using either the](https://docs.rs#min_time)

`min_time``DIVAN_MIN_TIME` environment variable
or `--min-time` CLI argument.Unless [ skip_ext_time](https://docs.rs#skip_ext_time) is set, this includes time external to the
benchmarked function, such as time spent generating inputs and running

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html)

`Drop````
use std::time::Duration;
#[divan::bench(min_time = Duration::from_secs(3))]
fn add() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
```
For convenience, [ min_time](https://docs.rs#min_time) can also be set with seconds as

[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)

`u64`[. Invalid values will cause a panic at runtime.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)

`f64````
#[divan::bench(min_time = 2)]
fn int_secs() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
#[divan::bench(min_time = 1.5)]
fn float_secs() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#max_time)`max_time`

The maximum time spent benchmarking each function can be set to a
predetermined [ Duration](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/time/struct.Duration.html) via the

[option. This may be overridden at runtime using either the](https://docs.rs#max_time)

`max_time``DIVAN_MAX_TIME` environment variable
or `--max-time` CLI argument.Unless [ skip_ext_time](https://docs.rs#skip_ext_time) is set, this includes time external to the
benchmarked function, such as time spent generating inputs and running

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html)

`Drop`If `min_time > max_time`, then [ max_time](https://docs.rs#max_time) has priority and

[will not be reached.](https://docs.rs#min_time)

`min_time````
use std::time::Duration;
#[divan::bench(max_time = Duration::from_secs(5))]
fn add() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
```
For convenience, like [ min_time](https://docs.rs#min_time),

[can also be set with seconds as](https://docs.rs#max_time)

`max_time`[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html)

`u64`[. Invalid values will cause a panic at runtime.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)

`f64````
#[divan::bench(max_time = 8)]
fn int_secs() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
#[divan::bench(max_time = 9.5)]
fn float_secs() -> i32 {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#skip_ext_time)`skip_ext_time`

By default, [ min_time](https://docs.rs#min_time) and

[include time external to the benchmarked function, such as time spent generating inputs and running](https://docs.rs#max_time)

`max_time`[. Enabling the](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/drop/trait.Drop.html)

`Drop`[option will instead make those options only consider time spent within the benchmarked function. This may be overridden at runtime using either the](https://docs.rs#skip_ext_time)

`skip_ext_time``DIVAN_SKIP_EXT_TIME` environment
variable or `--skip-ext-time` CLI argument.In the following example, [ max_time](https://docs.rs#max_time) only considers time spent running

`measured_function`:```
#[divan::bench(max_time = 5, skip_ext_time)]
fn bench(bencher: divan::Bencher) {
    bencher
        .with_inputs(|| generate_input())
        .bench_values(|input| measured_function(input));
}
```
This option can be set to an explicit [ bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) value to override parent
values:

```
#[divan::bench(max_time = 5, skip_ext_time = false)]
fn bench(bencher: divan::Bencher) {
    // ...
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#ignore)`ignore`

Like [ #[test]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/attributes/testing.html#the-test-attribute),

`#[divan::bench]` functions can use [:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/attributes/testing.html#the-ignore-attribute)

`#[ignore]````
#[divan::bench]
#[ignore]
fn todo() {
    unimplemented!();
}
```
This option can also instead be set within the `#[divan::bench]` attribute:

```
#[divan::bench(ignore)]
fn todo() {
    unimplemented!();
}
```
Like [ skip_ext_time](https://docs.rs#skip_ext_time), this option can be set to an explicit

[value to override parent values:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`bool````
#[divan::bench(ignore = false)]
fn bench() {
    // ...
}
```
This can be used to ignore benchmarks based on a runtime condition. The
following example benchmark will be ignored if an [environment
variable](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/env/fn.var.html) is not set to “true”:

```
#[divan::bench(
    ignore = std::env::var("BENCH_EXPENSIVE").as_deref() != Ok("true")
)]
fn expensive_bench() {
    // ...
}
```

# divan::counter - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/divan/0.1.21/divan/counter/index.html

## Expand description

Count values processed in each iteration to measure throughput.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

The following example measures throughput of converting
[ &[i32]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html) into

[by providing](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)

`Vec<i32>`[via](https://docs.rs/struct.BytesCount.html)

`BytesCount`[:](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html#method.counter)

`Bencher::counter````
use divan::counter::BytesCount;
#[divan::bench]
fn slice_into_vec(bencher: divan::Bencher) {
    let ints: &[i32] = &[
        // ...
    ];
    let bytes = BytesCount::of_slice(ints);
    bencher
        .counter(bytes)
        .bench(|| -> Vec<i32> {
            divan::black_box(ints).into()
        });
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.BytesCount.html)- Count
- Process N bytes.
- [Chars](https://docs.rs/struct.CharsCount.html)- Count
- Process N `char`s
- [Cycles](https://docs.rs/struct.CyclesCount.html)- Count
- Process N cycles, displayed as Hertz.
- [Items](https://docs.rs/struct.ItemsCount.html)- Count
- Process N items.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Bytes](https://docs.rs/enum.BytesFormat.html)- Format
- The numerical base for `BytesCount`

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Counter](https://docs.rs/trait.Counter.html)
- Counts the number of values processed in each iteration of a benchmarked function.
- [Into](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoCounter.html)- Counter
- Conversion into a `Counter`
