# value_parser in clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/^4/macro.value_parser.html

```
macro_rules! value_parser {
    ($name:ty) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Select a [ ValueParser](https://docs.rs/builder/struct.ValueParser.html) implementation from the intended type

Supported types

- `ValueParserFactory`types- [Native types](https://docs.rs/builder/struct.ValueParser.html):- `bool`,- `String`,- `OsString`,- `PathBuf`
- [Ranged numeric types](https://docs.rs/builder/struct.RangedI64ValueParser.html):- `u8`,- `i8`,- `u16`,- `i16`,- `u32`,- `i32`,- `u64`,- `i64`

- `ValueEnum`types
- `From<OsString>`types- `From<&OsStr>`types
- `From<String>`types- `From<&str>`types
- `FromStr`types

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Usage:

```
let mut cmd = clap::Command::new("raw")
    .arg(
        clap::Arg::new("output")
            .value_parser(clap::value_parser!(PathBuf))
            .required(true)
    );
let m = cmd.try_get_matches_from_mut(["cmd", "file.txt"]).unwrap();
let port: &PathBuf = m.get_one("output")
    .expect("required");
assert_eq!(port, Path::new("file.txt"));
```
Example mappings:

```
// Built-in types
let parser = clap::value_parser!(String);
assert_eq!(format!("{parser:?}"), "ValueParser::string");
let parser = clap::value_parser!(std::ffi::OsString);
assert_eq!(format!("{parser:?}"), "ValueParser::os_string");
let parser = clap::value_parser!(std::path::PathBuf);
assert_eq!(format!("{parser:?}"), "ValueParser::path_buf");
clap::value_parser!(u16).range(3000..);
clap::value_parser!(u64).range(3000..);
// FromStr types
let parser = clap::value_parser!(usize);
assert_eq!(format!("{parser:?}"), "_AnonymousValueParser(ValueParser::other(usize))");
// ValueEnum types
clap::value_parser!(ColorChoice);
```

# ArgGroup in clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/^4/struct.ArgGroup.html

`pub struct ArgGroup { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Specifies a logical group of [arguments](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)

You can use this for

- applying validation to an entire group, like `ArgGroup::multiple`
- validate relationships between an argument and a group, like [conflicts](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.conflicts_with)or[requirements](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.requires)
- check which argument in a group was specified on the command-line

For visually grouping arguments in help, see instead
[ Arg::help_heading](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.help_heading).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

The following example demonstrates using an `ArgGroup` to ensure that one, and only one, of
the arguments from the specified group is present at runtime.

```
let result = Command::new("cmd")
    .arg(arg!(--"set-ver" <ver> "set the version manually"))
    .arg(arg!(--major           "auto increase major"))
    .arg(arg!(--minor           "auto increase minor"))
    .arg(arg!(--patch           "auto increase patch"))
    .group(ArgGroup::new("vers")
         .args(["set-ver", "major", "minor", "patch"])
         .required(true))
    .try_get_matches_from(vec!["cmd", "--major", "--patch"]);
// Because we used two args in the group it's an error
assert!(result.is_err());
let err = result.unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), ErrorKind::ArgumentConflict);
```
This next example shows a passing parse of the same scenario

```
let result = Command::new("cmd")
    .arg(arg!(--"set-ver" <ver> "set the version manually"))
    .arg(arg!(--major           "auto increase major"))
    .arg(arg!(--minor           "auto increase minor"))
    .arg(arg!(--patch           "auto increase patch"))
    .group(ArgGroup::new("vers")
         .args(["set-ver", "major", "minor","patch"])
         .required(true))
    .try_get_matches_from(vec!["cmd", "--major"]);
assert!(result.is_ok());
let matches = result.unwrap();
// We may not know which of the args was used, so we can test for the group...
assert!(matches.contains_id("vers"));
// We can also ask the group which arg was used
assert_eq!(matches
    .get_one::<Id>("vers")
    .expect("`vers` is required")
    .as_str(),
    "major"
);
// we could also alternatively check each arg individually (not shown here)
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/builder/arg_group.rs.html#263)#### pub fn [is_multiple](https://docs.rs#method.is_multiple)(&mut self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/builder/arg_group.rs.html#263)

#### pub fn [is_multiple](https://docs.rs#method.is_multiple)(&mut self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Return true if the group allows more than one of the arguments
in this group to be used. (Default: `false`)

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

```
let mut group = ArgGroup::new("myprog")
    .args(["f", "c"])
    .multiple(true);
assert!(group.is_multiple());
```
Require an argument from the group to be present when parsing.

This is unless conflicting with another argument.  A required group will be displayed in
the usage string of the application in the format `<arg|arg2|arg3>`.

**NOTE:** By default, [ ArgGroup::multiple](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html#method.multiple) is set to

`false` which when combined with
`ArgGroup::required(true)` states, “One and *only one*arg must be used from this group. Use of more than one arg is an error.” Vice setting

`ArgGroup::multiple(true)` which
states, ’*At least*one arg from this group must be used. Using multiple is OK.“

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
let result = Command::new("myprog")
    .arg(Arg::new("flag")
        .short('f')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("color")
        .short('c')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .group(ArgGroup::new("req_flags")
        .args(["flag", "color"])
        .required(true))
    .try_get_matches_from(vec!["myprog"]);
// Because we didn't use any of the args in the group, it's an error
assert!(result.is_err());
let err = result.unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), ErrorKind::MissingRequiredArgument);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/builder/arg_group.rs.html#360)#### pub fn [requires](https://docs.rs#method.requires)(self, id: impl [IntoResettable](https://docs.rs/builder/trait.IntoResettable.html)<[Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)>) -> [ArgGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/builder/arg_group.rs.html#360)

#### pub fn [requires](https://docs.rs#method.requires)(self, id: impl [IntoResettable](https://docs.rs/builder/trait.IntoResettable.html)<[Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)>) -> [ArgGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html)

Specify an argument or group that must be present when this group is.

This is not to be confused with a [required group](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html#method.required). Requirement rules function just like
[argument requirement rules](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.requires), you can name other arguments or groups that must be present
when any one of the arguments from this group is used.

**NOTE:** The name provided may be an argument or group name

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
let result = Command::new("myprog")
    .arg(Arg::new("flag")
        .short('f')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("color")
        .short('c')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("debug")
        .short('d')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .group(ArgGroup::new("req_flags")
        .args(["flag", "color"])
        .requires("debug"))
    .try_get_matches_from(vec!["myprog", "-c"]);
// because we used an arg from the group, and the group requires "-d" to be used, it's an
// error
assert!(result.is_err());
let err = result.unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), ErrorKind::MissingRequiredArgument);
```

#### pub fn [requires_all](https://docs.rs#method.requires_all)(
    self,
    ns: impl [IntoIterator](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/iter/traits/collect/trait.IntoIterator.html)<Item = impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)>>,
) -> [ArgGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html)

Specify arguments or groups that must be present when this group is.

This is not to be confused with a [required group](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html#method.required). Requirement rules function just like
[argument requirement rules](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.requires_ifs), you can name other arguments or groups that must be present
when one of the arguments from this group is used.

**NOTE:** The names provided may be an argument or group name

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
let result = Command::new("myprog")
    .arg(Arg::new("flag")
        .short('f')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("color")
        .short('c')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("debug")
        .short('d')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("verb")
        .short('v')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .group(ArgGroup::new("req_flags")
        .args(["flag", "color"])
        .requires_all(["debug", "verb"]))
    .try_get_matches_from(vec!["myprog", "-c", "-d"]);
// because we used an arg from the group, and the group requires "-d" and "-v" to be used,
// yet we only used "-d" it's an error
assert!(result.is_err());
let err = result.unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), ErrorKind::MissingRequiredArgument);
```

# ArgMatches in clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/^4/struct.ArgMatches.html

`pub struct ArgMatches { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Container for parse results.

Used to get information about the arguments that were supplied to the program at runtime by
the user. New instances of this struct are obtained by using the [ Command::get_matches](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.get_matches) family of
methods.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let matches = Command::new("MyApp")
    .arg(Arg::new("out")
        .long("output")
        .required(true)
        .action(ArgAction::Set)
        .default_value("-"))
    .arg(Arg::new("cfg")
        .short('c')
        .action(ArgAction::Set))
    .get_matches(); // builds the instance of ArgMatches
// to get information about the "cfg" argument we created, such as the value supplied we use
// various ArgMatches methods, such as [ArgMatches::get_one]
if let Some(c) = matches.get_one::<String>("cfg") {
    println!("Value for -c: {c}");
}
// The ArgMatches::get_one method returns an Option because the user may not have supplied
// that argument at runtime. But if we specified that the argument was "required" as we did
// with the "out" argument, we can safely unwrap because `clap` verifies that was actually
// used at runtime.
println!("Value for --output: {}", matches.get_one::<String>("out").unwrap());
// You can check the presence of an argument's values
if matches.contains_id("out") {
    // However, if you want to know where the value came from
    if matches.value_source("out").expect("checked contains_id") == ValueSource::CommandLine {
        println!("`out` set by user");
    } else {
        println!("`out` is defaulted");
    }
}
```

### impl [ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html)

Gets the value of a specific option or positional argument.

i.e. an argument that [takes an additional value](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.num_args) at runtime.

Returns an error if the wrong type was used.

Returns `None` if the option wasn’t present.

*NOTE:* This will always return `Some(value)` if [ default_value](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.default_value) has been set.

[can be used to check if a value is present at runtime.](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html#method.value_source)

`ArgMatches::value_source`[§](https://docs.rs#panic)Panic

If the argument definition and access mismatch.  To handle this case programmatically, see
[ ArgMatches::try_get_one](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html#method.try_get_one).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("port")
        .value_parser(value_parser!(usize))
        .action(ArgAction::Set)
        .required(true))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "2020"]);
let port: usize = *m
    .get_one("port")
    .expect("`port`is required");
assert_eq!(port, 2020);
```
```

60fn main() {
61    let matches = cli().get_matches();
62
63    match matches.subcommand() {
64        Some(("clone", sub_matches)) => {
65            println!(
66                "Cloning {}",
67                sub_matches.get_one::<String>("REMOTE").expect("required")
68            );
69        }
70        Some(("diff", sub_matches)) => {
71            let color = sub_matches
72                .get_one::<String>("color")
73                .map(|s| s.as_str())
74                .expect("defaulted in clap");
75
76            let mut base = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("base").map(|s| s.as_str());
77            let mut head = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("head").map(|s| s.as_str());
78            let mut path = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("path").map(|s| s.as_str());
79            if path.is_none() {
80                path = head;
81                head = None;
82                if path.is_none() {
83                    path = base;
84                    base = None;
85                }
86            }
87            let base = base.unwrap_or("stage");
88            let head = head.unwrap_or("worktree");
89            let path = path.unwrap_or("");
90            println!("Diffing {base}..{head} {path} (color={color})");
91        }
92        Some(("push", sub_matches)) => {
93            println!(
94                "Pushing to {}",
95                sub_matches.get_one::<String>("REMOTE").expect("required")
96            );
97        }
98        Some(("add", sub_matches)) => {
99            let paths = sub_matches
100                .get_many::<PathBuf>("PATH")
101                .into_iter()
102                .flatten()
103                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
104            println!("Adding {paths:?}");
105        }
106        Some(("stash", sub_matches)) => {
107            let stash_command = sub_matches.subcommand().unwrap_or(("push", sub_matches));
108            match stash_command {
109                ("apply", sub_matches) => {
110                    let stash = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("STASH");
111                    println!("Applying {stash:?}");
112                }
113                ("pop", sub_matches) => {
114                    let stash = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("STASH");
115                    println!("Popping {stash:?}");
116                }
117                ("push", sub_matches) => {
118                    let message = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("message");
119                    println!("Pushing {message:?}");
120                }
121                (name, _) => {
122                    unreachable!("Unsupported subcommand `{name}`")
123                }
124            }
125        }
126        Some((ext, sub_matches)) => {
127            let args = sub_matches
128                .get_many::<OsString>("")
129                .into_iter()
130                .flatten()
131                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
132            println!("Calling out to {ext:?} with {args:?}");
133        }
134        _ => unreachable!(), // If all subcommands are defined above, anything else is unreachable!()
135    }
136
137    // Continued program logic goes here...
138}

16    fn from_arg_matches_mut(matches: &mut ArgMatches) -> Result<Self, Error> {
17        Ok(Self {
18            foo: matches.get_flag("foo"),
19            bar: matches.get_flag("bar"),
20            quuz: matches.remove_one::<String>("quuz"),
21        })
22    }
23    fn update_from_arg_matches(&mut self, matches: &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), Error> {
24        let mut matches = matches.clone();
25        self.update_from_arg_matches_mut(&mut matches)
26    }
27    fn update_from_arg_matches_mut(&mut self, matches: &mut ArgMatches) -> Result<(), Error> {
28        self.foo |= matches.get_flag("foo");
29        self.bar |= matches.get_flag("bar");
30        if let Some(quuz) = matches.remove_one::<String>("quuz") {
31            self.quuz = Some(quuz);
32        }
33        Ok(())
34    }

71    match matches.subcommand() {
72        Some(("sync", sync_matches)) => {

74                let packages: Vec<_> = sync_matches
75                    .get_many::<String>("search")
76                    .expect("contains_id")
77                    .map(|s| s.as_str())
78                    .collect();
79                let values = packages.join(", ");
80                println!("Searching for {values}...");
81                return;
82            }
83

85                .get_many::<String>("package")
86                .expect("is present")
87                .map(|s| s.as_str())
88                .collect();

90

100                println!("Retrieving info for {comma_sep}...");
101            } else if let Some(queries) = query_matches.get_many::<String>("search") {
102                let comma_sep = queries.map(|s| s.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
103                println!("Searching Locally for {comma_sep}...");
104            } else {
105                println!("Displaying all locally installed packages...");
106            }
107        }
108        _ => unreachable!(), // If all subcommands are defined above, anything else is unreachable
109    }

105        }
106        Some(("stash", sub_matches)) => {
107            let stash_command = sub_matches.subcommand().unwrap_or(("push", sub_matches));
108            match stash_command {
109                ("apply", sub_matches) => {
110                    let stash = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("STASH");
111                    println!("Applying {stash:?}");
112                }
113                ("pop", sub_matches) => {
114                    let stash = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("STASH");
115                    println!("Popping {stash:?}");
116                }
117                ("push", sub_matches) => {
118                    let message = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("message");
119                    println!("Pushing {message:?}");
120                }
121                (name, _) => {
122                    unreachable!("Unsupported subcommand `{name}`")
123                }
124            }
125        }
126        Some((ext, sub_matches)) => {
127            let args = sub_matches
128                .get_many::<OsString>("")
129                .into_iter()
130                .flatten()
131                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
132            println!("Calling out to {ext:?} with {args:?}");
133        }
134        _ => unreachable!(), // If all subcommands are defined above, anything else is unreachable!()
135    }
136
137    // Continued program logic goes here...
138}
```

106            }
107        }
108        _ => unreachable!(), // If all subcommands are defined above, anything else is unreachable

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/parser/matches/arg_matches.rs.html#263-266)#### pub fn [get_occurrences](https://docs.rs#method.get_occurrences)<T>(&self, id: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<OccurrencesRef<'_, T>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/parser/matches/arg_matches.rs.html#263-266)

#### pub fn [get_occurrences](https://docs.rs#method.get_occurrences)<T>(&self, id: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<OccurrencesRef<'_, T>>

Iterate over the values passed to each occurrence of an option.

Each item is itself an iterator containing the arguments passed to a single occurrence of the option.

If the option doesn’t support multiple occurrences, or there was only a single occurrence, the iterator will only contain a single item.

Returns `None` if the option wasn’t present.

[§](https://docs.rs#panics)Panics

If the argument definition and access mismatch (debug builds). To handle this case programmatically, see
[ ArgMatches::try_get_occurrences](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html#method.try_get_occurrences).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
let m = Command::new("myprog")
    .arg(Arg::new("x")
        .short('x')
        .num_args(2)
        .action(ArgAction::Append)
        .value_parser(value_parser!(String)))
    .get_matches_from(vec![
        "myprog", "-x", "a", "b", "-x", "c", "d"]);
let vals: Vec<Vec<&String>> = m.get_occurrences("x").unwrap().map(Iterator::collect).collect();
assert_eq!(vals, [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]]);
```
Iterate over the original argument values.

An `OsStr` on Unix-like systems is any series of bytes, regardless of whether or not they
contain valid UTF-8. Since [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)s in Rust are guaranteed to be valid UTF-8, a valid
filename on a Unix system as an argument value may contain invalid UTF-8.

Returns `None` if the option wasn’t present.

[§](https://docs.rs#panic-4)Panic

If the argument definition and access mismatch.  To handle this case programmatically, see
[ ArgMatches::try_get_raw](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html#method.try_get_raw).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
use std::path::PathBuf;
let m = Command::new("utf8")
    .arg(arg!(<arg> ... "some arg").value_parser(value_parser!(PathBuf)))
    .get_matches_from(vec![OsString::from("myprog"),
                                // "Hi"
                                OsString::from_vec(vec![b'H', b'i']),
                                // "{0xe9}!"
                                OsString::from_vec(vec![0xe9, b'!'])]);
let mut itr = m.get_raw("arg")
    .expect("`port`is required")
    .into_iter();
assert_eq!(itr.next(), Some(OsStr::new("Hi")));
assert_eq!(itr.next(), Some(OsStr::from_bytes(&[0xe9, b'!'])));
assert_eq!(itr.next(), None);
```

Iterate over the original values for each occurrence of an option.

Similar to [ ArgMatches::get_occurrences](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html#method.get_occurrences) but returns raw values.

An `OsStr` on Unix-like systems is any series of bytes, regardless of whether or not they
contain valid UTF-8. Since [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)s in Rust are guaranteed to be valid UTF-8, a valid
filename on a Unix system as an argument value may contain invalid UTF-8.

Returns `None` if the option wasn’t present.

[§](https://docs.rs#panic-5)Panic

If the argument definition and access mismatch.  To handle this case programmatically, see
[ ArgMatches::try_get_raw_occurrences](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html#method.try_get_raw_occurrences).

16    fn from_arg_matches_mut(matches: &mut ArgMatches) -> Result<Self, Error> {
17        Ok(Self {
18            foo: matches.get_flag("foo"),
19            bar: matches.get_flag("bar"),
20            quuz: matches.remove_one::<String>("quuz"),
21        })
22    }
23    fn update_from_arg_matches(&mut self, matches: &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), Error> {
24        let mut matches = matches.clone();
25        self.update_from_arg_matches_mut(&mut matches)
26    }
27    fn update_from_arg_matches_mut(&mut self, matches: &mut ArgMatches) -> Result<(), Error> {
28        self.foo |= matches.get_flag("foo");
29        self.bar |= matches.get_flag("bar");
30        if let Some(quuz) = matches.remove_one::<String>("quuz") {
31            self.quuz = Some(quuz);
32        }
33        Ok(())
34    }

        .map(|id| id.as_str())
        .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    ["config", "color"]
);
```

Report where argument value came from

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-2)Panics

If `id` is not a valid argument or group id (debug builds).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

```
let m = Command::new("myprog")
    .arg(Arg::new("debug")
        .short('d')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .get_matches_from(vec![
        "myprog", "-d"

The first index of that an argument showed up.

Indices are similar to argv indices, but are not exactly 1:1.

For flags (i.e. those arguments which don’t have an associated value), indices refer
to occurrence of the switch, such as `-f`, or `--flag`. However, for options the indices
refer to the *values* `-o val` would therefore not represent two distinct indices, only the
index for `val` would be recorded. This is by design.

Besides the flag/option discrepancy, the primary difference between an argv index and clap index, is that clap continues counting once all arguments have properly separated, whereas an argv index does not.

The examples should clear this up.

*NOTE:* If an argument is allowed multiple times, this method will only give the *first*
index.  See [ ArgMatches::indices_of](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html#method.indices_of).

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-3)Panics

If `id` is not a valid argument or group id (debug builds).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

The argv indices are listed in the comments below. See how they correspond to the clap
indices. Note that if it’s not listed in a clap index, this is because it’s not saved in
in an `ArgMatches` struct for querying.

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("flag")
        .short('f')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("option")
        .short('o')
        .action(ArgAction::Set))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "-f", "-o", "val"]);
           // ARGV indices: ^0       ^1    ^2    ^3
           // clap indices:          ^1          ^3
assert_eq!(m.index_of("flag"), Some(1));
assert_eq!(m.index_of("option"), Some(3));
```
Now notice, if we use one of the other styles of options:

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("flag")
        .short('f')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("option")
        .short('o')
        .action(ArgAction::Set))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "-f", "-o=val"]);
           // ARGV indices: ^0       ^1    ^2
           // clap indices:          ^1       ^3
assert_eq!(m.index_of("flag"), Some(1));
assert_eq!(m.index_of("option"), Some(3));
```
Things become much more complicated, or clear if we look at a more complex combination of flags. Let’s also throw in the final option style for good measure.

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("flag")
        .short('f')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("flag2")
        .short('F')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("flag3")
        .short('z')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("option")
        .short('o')
        .action(ArgAction::Set))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "-fzF", "-oval"]);
           // ARGV indices: ^0      ^1       ^2
           // clap indices:         ^1,2,3    ^5
           //
           // clap sees the above as 'myapp -f -z -F -o val'
           //                         ^0    ^1 ^2 ^3 ^4 ^5
assert_eq!(m.index_of("flag"), Some(1));
assert_eq!(m.index_of("flag2"), Some(3));
assert_eq!(m.index_of("flag3"), Some(2));
assert_eq!(m.index_of("option"), Some(5));
```
One final combination of flags/options to see how they combine:

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("flag")
        .short('f')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("flag2")
        .short('F')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("flag3")
        .short('z')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue))
    .arg(Arg::new("option")
        .short('o')
        .action(ArgAction::Set))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "-fzFoval"]);
           // ARGV indices: ^0       ^1
           // clap indices:          ^1,2,3^5
           //
           // clap sees the above as 'myapp -f -z -F -o val'
           //                         ^0    ^1 ^2 ^3 ^4 ^5
assert_eq!(m.index_of("flag"), Some(1));
assert_eq!(m.index_of("flag2"), Some(3));
assert_eq!(m.index_of("flag3"), Some(2));
assert_eq!(m.index_of("option"), Some(5));
```
The last part to mention is when values are sent in multiple groups with a [delimiter](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.value_delimiter).

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("option")
        .short('o')
        .value_delimiter(',')
        .num_args(1..))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "-o=val1,val2,val3"]);
           // ARGV indices: ^0       ^1
           // clap indices:             ^2   ^3   ^4
           //
           // clap sees the above as 'myapp -o val1 val2 val3'
           //                         ^0    ^1 ^2   ^3   ^4
assert_eq!(m.index_of("option"), Some(2));
assert_eq!(m.indices_of("option").unwrap().collect::<Vec<_>>(), &[2, 3, 4]);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/parser/matches/arg_matches.rs.html#855)#### pub fn [indices_of](https://docs.rs#method.indices_of)(&self, id: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Indices](https://docs.rs/parser/struct.Indices.html)<'_>>

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/parser/matches/arg_matches.rs.html#855)

#### pub fn [indices_of](https://docs.rs#method.indices_of)(&self, id: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Indices](https://docs.rs/parser/struct.Indices.html)<'_>>

All indices an argument appeared at when parsing.

Indices are similar to argv indices, but are not exactly 1:1.

For flags (i.e. those arguments which don’t have an associated value), indices refer
to occurrence of the switch, such as `-f`, or `--flag`. However, for options the indices
refer to the *values* `-o val` would therefore not represent two distinct indices, only the
index for `val` would be recorded. This is by design.

*NOTE:* For more information about how clap indices compared to argv indices, see
`ArgMatches::index_of`

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-4)Panics

If `id` is not a valid argument or group id (debug builds).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-16)Examples

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("option")
        .short('o')
        .value_delimiter(','))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "-o=val1,val2,val3"]);
           // ARGV indices: ^0       ^1
           // clap indices:             ^2   ^3   ^4
           //
           // clap sees the above as 'myapp -o val1 val2 val3'
           //                         ^0    ^1 ^2   ^3   ^4
assert_eq!(m.indices_of("option").unwrap().collect::<Vec<_>>(), &[2, 3, 4]);
```
Another quick example is when flags and options are used together

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("option")
        .short('o')
        .action(ArgAction::Set)
        .action(ArgAction::Append))
    .arg(Arg::new("flag")
        .short('f')
        .action(ArgAction::Count))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "-o", "val1", "-f", "-o", "val2", "-f"]);
           // ARGV indices: ^0       ^1    ^2      ^3    ^4    ^5      ^6
           // clap indices:                ^2      ^3          ^5      ^6
assert_eq!(m.indices_of("option").unwrap().collect::<Vec<_>>(), &[2, 5]);
assert_eq!(m.indices_of("flag").unwrap().collect::<Vec<_>>(), &[6]);
```
One final example, which is an odd case; if we *don’t* use  value delimiter as we did with
the first example above instead of `val1`, `val2` and `val3` all being distinc values, they
would all be a single value of `val1,val2,val3`, in which case they’d only receive a single
index.

```
let m = Command::new("myapp")
    .arg(Arg::new("option")
        .short('o')
        .action(ArgAction::Set)
        .num_args(1..))
    .get_matches_from(vec!["myapp", "-o=val1,val2,val3"]);
           // ARGV indices: ^0       ^1
           // clap indices:             ^2
           //
           // clap sees the above as 'myapp -o "val1,val2,val3"'
           //                         ^0    ^1  ^2
assert_eq!(m.indices_of("option").unwrap().collect::<Vec<_>>(), &[2]);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/parser/matches/arg_matches.rs.html#922)#### pub fn [subcommand](https://docs.rs#method.subcommand)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &[ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html))>

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/parser/matches/arg_matches.rs.html#922)

#### pub fn [subcommand](https://docs.rs#method.subcommand)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<(&[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &[ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html))>

The name and `ArgMatches` of the current [subcommand](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.subcommand).

Subcommand values are put in a child `ArgMatches`

Returns `None` if the subcommand wasn’t present at runtime,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-17)Examples

```
 let app_m = Command::new("git")
     .subcommand(Command::new("clone"))
     .subcommand(Command::new("push"))
     .subcommand(Command::new("commit"))
     .get_matches();
match app_m.subcommand() {
    Some(("clone",  sub_m)) => {}, // clone was used
    Some(("push",   sub_m)) => {}, // push was used
    Some(("commit", sub_m)) => {}, // commit was used
    _                       => {}, // Either no subcommand or one not tested for...
}
```
Another useful scenario is when you want to support third party, or external, subcommands. In these cases you can’t know the subcommand name ahead of time, so use a variable instead with pattern matching!

```
// Assume there is an external subcommand named "subcmd"
let app_m = Command::new("myprog")
    .allow_external_subcommands(true)
    .get_matches_from(vec![
        "myprog", "subcmd", "--option", "value", "-fff", "--flag"
    ]);
// All trailing arguments will be stored under the subcommand's sub-matches using an empty
// string argument name
match app_m.subcommand() {
    Some((external, sub_m)) => {
         let ext_args: Vec<&OsStr> = sub_m.get_many::<OsString>("")
            .unwrap().map(|s| s.as_os_str()).collect();
         assert_eq!(external, "subcmd");
         assert_eq!(ext_args, ["--option", "value", "-fff", "--flag"]);
    },
    _ => {},
}
```
```
23    fn from_arg_matches(matches: &ArgMatches) -> Result<Self, Error> {
24        match matches.subcommand() {
25            Some(("add", args)) => Ok(Self::Add(AddArgs::from_arg_matches(args)?)),
26            Some(("remove", args)) => Ok(Self::Remove(RemoveArgs::from_arg_matches(args)?)),
27            Some((_, _)) => Err(Error::raw(
28                ErrorKind::InvalidSubcommand,
29                "Valid subcommands are `add` and `remove`",
30            )),
31            None => Err(Error::raw(
32                ErrorKind::MissingSubcommand,
33                "Valid subcommands are `add` and `remove`",
34            )),
35        }
36    }
37    fn update_from_arg_matches(&mut self, matches: &ArgMatches) -> Result<(), Error> {
38        match matches.subcommand() {
39            Some(("add", args)) => *self = Self::Add(AddArgs::from_arg_matches(args)?),
40            Some(("remove", args)) => *self = Self::Remove(RemoveArgs::from_arg_matches(args)?),
41            Some((_, _)) => {
42                return Err(Error::raw(
43                    ErrorKind::InvalidSubcommand,
44                    "Valid subcommands are `add` and `remove`",
45                ));
46            }
47            None => (),
48        };
49        Ok(())
50    }
```

29fn respond(line: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {
30    let args = shlex::split(line).ok_or("error: Invalid quoting")?;
31    let matches = cli()
32        .try_get_matches_from(args)
33        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
34    match matches.subcommand() {
35        Some(("ping", _matches)) => {
36            write!(std::io::stdout(), "Pong").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
37            std::io::stdout().flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
38        }
39        Some(("quit", _matches)) => {
40            write!(std::io::stdout(), "Exiting ...").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
41            std::io::stdout().flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
42            return Ok(true);
43        }
44        Some((name, _matches)) => unimplemented!("{name}"),
45        None => unreachable!("subcommand required"),
46    }
47
48    Ok(false)
49}

13fn main() {

60fn main() {
61    let matches = cli().get_matches();
62
63    match matches.subcommand() {
64        Some(("clone", sub_matches)) => {
65            println!(
66                "Cloning {}",
67                sub_matches.get_one::<String>("REMOTE").expect("required")
68            );
69        }
70        Some(("diff", sub_matches)) => {
71            let color = sub_matches
72                .get_one::<String>("color")
73                .map(|s| s.as_str())
74                .expect("defaulted in clap");
75
76            let mut base = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("base").map(|s| s.as_str());
77            let mut head = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("head").map(|s| s.as_str());
78            let mut path = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("path").map(|s| s.as_str());
79            if path.is_none() {
80                path = head;
81                head = None;
82                if path.is_none() {
83                    path = base;
84                    base = None;
85                }
86            }
87            let base = base.unwrap_or("stage");
88            let head = head.unwrap_or("worktree");
89            let path = path.unwrap_or("");
90            println!("Diffing {base}..{head} {path} (color={color})");
91        }
92        Some(("push", sub_matches)) => {
93            println!(
94                "Pushing to {}",
95                sub_matches.get_one::<String>("REMOTE").expect("required")
96            );
97        }
98        Some(("add", sub_matches)) => {
99            let paths = sub_matches
100                .get_many::<PathBuf>("PATH")
101                .into_iter()
102                .flatten()
103                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
104            println!("Adding {paths:?}");
105        }
106        Some(("stash", sub_matches)) => {
107            let stash_command = sub_matches.subcommand().unwrap_or(("push", sub_matches));
108            match stash_command {
109                ("apply", sub_matches) => {
110                    let stash = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("STASH");
111                    println!("Applying {stash:?}");
112                }
113                ("pop", sub_matches) => {
114                    let stash = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("STASH");
115                    println!("Popping {stash:?}");
116                }
117                ("push", sub_matches) => {
118                    let message = sub_matches.get_one::<String>("message");
119                    println!("Pushing {message:?}");
120                }
121                (name, _) => {
122                    unreachable!("Unsupported subcommand `{name}`")
123                }
124            }
125        }
126        Some((ext, sub_matches)) => {
127            let args = sub_matches
128                .get_many::<OsString>("")
129                .into_iter()
130                .flatten()
131                .collect::<Vec<_>>();
132            println!("Calling out to {ext:?} with {args:?}");
133        }
134        _ => unreachable!(), // If all subcommands are defined above, anything else is unreachable!()
135    }
136
137    // Continued program logic goes here...
138}

3fn main() {
4    let matches = Command::new("pacman")
5        .about("package manager utility")
6        .version("5.2.1")
7        .subcommand_required(true)
8        .arg_required_else_help(true)
9        // Query subcommand
10        //
11        // Only a few of its arguments are implemented below.
12        .subcommand(
13            Command::new("query")
14                .short_flag('Q')
15                .long_flag("query")
16                .about("Query the package database.")
17                .arg(
18                    Arg::new("search")
19                        .short('s')
20                        .long("search")
21                        .help("search locally installed packages for matching strings")
22                        .conflicts_with("info")
23                        .action(ArgAction::Set)
24                        .num_args(1..),
25                )
26                .arg(
27                    Arg::new("info")
28                        .long("info")
29                        .short('i')
30                        .conflicts_with("search")
31                        .help("view package information")
32                        .action(ArgAction::Set)
33                        .num_args(1..),
34                ),
35        )
36        // Sync subcommand
37        //
38        // Only a few of its arguments are implemented below.
39        .subcommand(
40            Command::new("sync")
41                .short_flag('S')
42                .long_flag("sync")
43                .about("Synchronize packages.")
44                .arg(
45                    Arg::new("search")
46                        .short('s')
47                        .long("search")
48                        .conflicts_with("info")
49                        .action(ArgAction::Set)
50                        .num_args(1..)
51                        .help("search remote repositories for matching strings"),
52                )
53                .arg(
54                    Arg::new("info")
55                        .long("info")
56                        .conflicts_with("search")
57                        .short('i')
58                        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
59                        .help("view package information"),
60                )
61                .arg(
62                    Arg::new("package")
63                        .help("packages")
64                        .required_unless_present("search")
65                        .action(ArgAction::Set)
66                        .num_args(1..),
67                ),
68        )
69        .get_matches();
70
71    match matches.subcommand() {
72        Some(("sync", sync_matches)) => {
73            if sync_matches.contains_id("search") {
74                let packages: Vec<_> = sync_matches
75                    .get_many::<String>("search")
76                    .expect("contains_id")
77                    .map(|s| s.as_str())
78                    .collect();
79                let values = packages.join(", ");
80                println!("Searching for {values}...");
81                return;
82            }
83
84            let packages: Vec<_> = sync_matches
85                .get_many::<String>("package")
86                .expect("is present")
87                .map(|s| s.as_str())
88                .collect();
89            let values = packages.join(", ");
90
91            if sync_matches.get_flag("info") {
92                println!("Retrieving info for {values}...");
93            } else {
94                println!("Installing {values}...");
95            }
96        }
97        Some(("query", query_matches)) => {
98            if let Some(packages) = query_matches.get_many::<String>("info") {
99                let comma_sep = packages.map(|s| s.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
100                println!("Retrieving info for {comma_sep}...");
101            } else if let Some(queries) = query_matches.get_many::<String>("search") {
102                let comma_sep = queries.map(|s| s.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
103                println!("Searching Locally for {comma_sep}...");
104            } else {
105                println!("Displaying all locally installed packages...");
106            }
107        }
108        _ => unreachable!(), // If all subcommands are defined above, anything else is unreachable
109    }
110}

[Source](https://docs.rs/clap_builder/4.6.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/src/clap_builder/parser/matches/arg_matches.rs.html#982)

#### pub fn [remove_subcommand](https://docs.rs#method.remove_subcommand)(&mut self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html))>

Return the name and `ArgMatches` of the current [subcommand](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.subcommand).

Subcommand values are put in a child `ArgMatches`

Returns `None` if the subcommand wasn’t present at runtime,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
 let mut app_m = Command::new("git")
     .subcommand(Command::new("clone"))
     .subcommand(Command::new("push"))
     .subcommand(Command::new("commit"))
     .subcommand_required(true)
     .get_matches();
let (name, sub_m) = app_m.remove_subcommand().expect("required");
match (name.as_str(), sub_m) {
    ("clone",  sub_m) => {}, // clone was used
    ("push",   sub_m) => {}, // push was used
    ("commit", sub_m) => {}, // commit was used
    (name, _)         => unimplemented!("{name}"),
}
```
Another useful scenario is when you want to support third party, or external, subcommands. In these cases you can’t know the subcommand name ahead of time, so use a variable instead with pattern matching!

```
// Assume there is an external subcommand named "subcmd"
let mut app_m = Command::new("myprog")
    .allow_external_subcommands(true)
    .get_matches_from(vec![
        "myprog", "subcmd", "--option", "value", "-fff", "--flag"
    ]);
// All trailing arguments will be stored under the subcommand's sub-matches using an empty
// string argument name
match app_m.remove_subcommand() {
    Some((external, mut sub_m)) => {
         let ext_args: Vec<OsString> = sub_m.remove_many("")
            .expect("`file`is required")
            .collect();
         assert_eq!(external, "subcmd");
         assert_eq!(ext_args, ["--option", "value", "-fff", "--flag"]);
    },
    _ => {},
}
```

The `ArgMatches` for the current [subcommand](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.subcommand).

Subcommand values are put in a child `ArgMatches`

Returns `None` if the subcommand wasn’t present at runtime,

[§](https://docs.rs#panics-5)Panics

If `id` is not a valid subcommand (debug builds).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-19)Examples

```
let app_m = Command::new("myprog")
    .arg(Arg::new("debug")
        .short('d')
        .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
    )
    .subcommand(Command::new("test")
        .arg(Arg::new("opt")
            .long("option")
            .action(ArgAction::Set)))
    .get_matches_from(vec![
        "myprog", "-d", "test", "--option", "val"
    ]);
// Both parent commands, and child subcommands can have arguments present at the same times
assert!(app_m.get_flag("debug"));
// Get the subcommand's ArgMatches instance
if let Some(sub_m) = app_m.subcommand_matches("test") {
    // Use the struct like normal
    assert_eq!(sub_m.get_one::<String>("opt").map(|s| s.as_str()), Some("val"));
}

Clears the values for the given `id`

Alternative to [ try_remove_*](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html#method.try_remove_one) when the type is not known.

Returns `Err([``MatchesError``])` if the given `id` isn’t valid for current `ArgMatches` instance.

Returns `Ok(true)` if there were any matches with the given `id`, `Ok(false)` otherwise.

# ArgAction in clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/^4/enum.ArgAction.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum ArgAction {
    Set,
    Append,
    SetTrue,
    SetFalse,
    Count,
    Help,
    HelpShort,
    HelpLong,
    Version,
}
```
## Expand description

Behavior of arguments when they are encountered while parsing

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("special-help")
            .short('?')
            .action(clap::ArgAction::Help)
    );
// Existing help still exists
let err = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "-h"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp);
// New help available
let err = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "-?"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp);
```
## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Set)

### Set

When encountered, store the associated value(s) in `ArgMatches`

**NOTE:** If the argument has previously been seen, it will result in a
[ ArgumentConflict](https://docs.rs/error/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.ArgumentConflict) unless

[is set.](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.args_override_self)

`Command::args_override_self(true)`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("flag")
            .long("flag")
            .action(clap::ArgAction::Set)
    );
let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "--flag", "value"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_many::<String>("flag").unwrap_or_default().map(|v| v.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    vec!["value"]
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Append)

### Append

When encountered, store the associated value(s) in `ArgMatches`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("flag")
            .long("flag")
            .action(clap::ArgAction::Append)
    );
let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "--flag", "value1", "--flag", "value2"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_many::<String>("flag").unwrap_or_default().map(|v| v.as_str()).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    vec!["value1", "value2"]
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SetTrue)

### SetTrue

When encountered, act as if `"true"` was encountered on the command-line

If no [ default_value](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.default_value) is set, it will be

`false`.No value is allowed. To optionally accept a value, see
`Arg::default_missing_value`

**NOTE:** If the argument has previously been seen, it will result in a
[ ArgumentConflict](https://docs.rs/error/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.ArgumentConflict) unless

[is set.](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.args_override_self)

`Command::args_override_self(true)`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("flag")
            .long("flag")
            .action(clap::ArgAction::SetTrue)
    );
let matches = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "--flag"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_flag("flag"),
    true
);
let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_flag("flag"),
    false
);
```
You can use [ TypedValueParser::map](https://docs.rs/builder/trait.TypedValueParser.html#method.map) to have the
flag control an application-specific type:

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("flag")
            .long("flag")
            .action(clap::ArgAction::SetTrue)
            .value_parser(
                BoolishValueParser::new()
                .map(|b| -> usize {
                    if b { 10 } else { 5 }
                })
            )
    );
let matches = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "--flag"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_one::<usize>("flag").copied(),
    Some(10)
);
let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_one::<usize>("flag").copied(),
    Some(5)
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.SetFalse)

### SetFalse

When encountered, act as if `"false"` was encountered on the command-line

If no [ default_value](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.default_value) is set, it will be

`true`.No value is allowed. To optionally accept a value, see
`Arg::default_missing_value`

**NOTE:** If the argument has previously been seen, it will result in a
[ ArgumentConflict](https://docs.rs/error/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.ArgumentConflict) unless

[is set.](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.args_override_self)

`Command::args_override_self(true)`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("flag")
            .long("flag")
            .action(clap::ArgAction::SetFalse)
    );
let matches = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "--flag"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_flag("flag"),
    false
);
let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_flag("flag"),
    true
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Count)

### Count

When encountered, increment a `u8` counter starting from `0`.

If no [ default_value](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.default_value) is set, it will be

`0`.No value is allowed. To optionally accept a value, see
`Arg::default_missing_value`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-5)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("flag")
            .long("flag")
            .action(clap::ArgAction::Count)
    );
let matches = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "--flag", "--flag"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_count("flag"),
    2
);
let matches = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd"]).unwrap();
assert!(matches.contains_id("flag"));
assert_eq!(
    matches.get_count("flag"),
    0
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Help)

### Help

When encountered, display `Command::print_help`

Depending on the flag, [ Command::print_long_help](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.print_long_help) may be shown

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-6)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("special-help")
            .short('?')
            .action(clap::ArgAction::Help)
    );
// Existing help still exists
let err = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "-h"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp);
// New help available
let err = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "-?"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.HelpShort)

### HelpShort

When encountered, display `Command::print_help`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("special-help")
            .short('?')
            .action(clap::ArgAction::HelpShort)
    );
// Existing help still exists
let err = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "-h"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp);
// New help available
let err = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "-?"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.HelpLong)

### HelpLong

When encountered, display `Command::print_long_help`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("special-help")
            .short('?')
            .action(clap::ArgAction::HelpLong)
    );
// Existing help still exists
let err = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "-h"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp);
// New help available

assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayHelp);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Version)

### Version

When encountered, display `Command::version`

Depending on the flag, [ Command::long_version](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.long_version) may be shown

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-9)Examples

```
let cmd = Command::new("mycmd")
    .version("1.0.0")
    .arg(
        Arg::new("special-version")
            .long("special-version")
            .action(clap::ArgAction::Version)
    );
// Existing version still exists
let err = cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "--version"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayVersion);
// New version available
let err = cmd.try_get_matches_from(["mycmd", "--special-version"]).unwrap_err();
assert_eq!(err.kind(), clap::error::ErrorKind::DisplayVersion);
```

Represents the color preferences for program output

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

# ValueHint in clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/^4/enum.ValueHint.html

```
#[non_exhaustive]pub enum ValueHint {
```
## Show 13 variants

    Unknown,
    Other,
    AnyPath,
    FilePath,
    DirPath,
    ExecutablePath,
    CommandName,
    CommandString,
    CommandWithArguments,
    Username,
    Hostname,
    Url,
    EmailAddress,
}## Expand description

Provide shell with hint on how to complete an argument.

See [ Arg::value_hint](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.value_hint) to set this on an argument.

See the `clap_complete` crate for completion script generation.

Overview of which hints are supported by which shell:

| Hint | zsh | fish [1](https://docs.rs#fn1) | dynamic |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AnyPath` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `FilePath` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `DirPath` | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `ExecutablePath` | Yes | Partial | Yes |
| `CommandName` | Yes | Yes | No |
| `CommandString` | Yes | Partial | No |
| `CommandWithArguments` | Yes | No | |
| `Username` | Yes | Yes | No |
| `Hostname` | Yes | Yes | No |
| `Url` | Yes | No | |
| `EmailAddress` | Yes | No |

## Variants (Non-exhaustive)[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

## This enum is marked as non-exhaustive

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Unknown)

### Unknown

Default value if hint is not specified. Follows shell default behavior, which is usually auto-completing filenames.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Other)

### Other

None of the hints below apply. Disables shell completion for this argument.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.AnyPath)

### AnyPath

Any existing path.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.FilePath)

### FilePath

Path to a file.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DirPath)

### DirPath

Path to a directory.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ExecutablePath)

### ExecutablePath

Path to an executable file.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CommandName)

### CommandName

Name of a command, without arguments. May be relative to PATH, or full path to executable.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CommandString)

### CommandString

A single string containing a command and its arguments.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CommandWithArguments)

### CommandWithArguments

Capture the remaining arguments as a command name and arguments for that command. This is
common when writing shell wrappers that execute another command, for example `sudo` or `env`.

This hint is special, the argument must be a positional argument and have
[ .num_args(1..)](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html#method.num_args) and Command must use

[. The result is that the command line](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html#method.trailing_var_arg)

`Command::trailing_var_arg(true)``my_app ls -la /` will be parsed as `["ls", "-la", "/"]` and clap won’t try to
parse the `-la` argument itself.[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Username)

### Username

Name of a local operating system user.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hostname)

### Hostname

Host name of a computer.
Shells usually parse `/etc/hosts` and `.ssh/known_hosts` to complete hostnames.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Url)

### Url

Complete web address.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.EmailAddress)

### EmailAddress

Email address.

#### fn [from_arg_matches](https://docs.rs#tymethod.from_arg_matches)(matches: &[ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<Self, [Error](https://docs.rs/error/struct.Error.html)>

Instantiate `Self` from [ ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html), parsing the arguments as needed.

Motivation: If our application had two CLI options, `--name <STRING>` and the flag `--debug`, we may create a struct as follows:

```
struct Context {
    name: String,
    debug: bool
}
```
We then need to convert the `ArgMatches` that `clap` generated into our struct.
`from_arg_matches` serves as the equivalent of:

```
impl From<ArgMatches> for Context {
   fn from(m: ArgMatches) -> Self {
       Context {
           name: m.get_one::<String>("name").unwrap().clone(),
           debug: m.get_flag("debug"),
       }
   }
}
```

}## Expand description

Parse command-line arguments into `Self`.

The primary one-stop-shop trait used to create an instance of a `clap`
[ Command](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html), conduct the parsing, and turn the resulting

[back into concrete instance of the user struct.](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html)

`ArgMatches`This trait is primarily a convenience on top of [ FromArgMatches](https://docs.rs/trait.FromArgMatches.html) +

[which uses those two underlying traits to build the two fundamental functions](https://docs.rs/trait.CommandFactory.html)

`CommandFactory``parse` which uses the `std::env::args_os` iterator,
and `parse_from` which allows the consumer to supply the iterator (along
with fallible options for each).See also [ Subcommand](https://docs.rs/trait.Subcommand.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.Args.html)

`Args`**NOTE:** Deriving requires the `derive` feature flag

Parse from iterator, return Err on error.

```
29fn respond(line: &str) -> Result<bool, String> {
30    let args = shlex::split(line).ok_or("error: Invalid quoting")?;
31    let cli = Cli::try_parse_from(args).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
32    match cli.command {
33        Commands::Ping => {
34            write!(std::io::stdout(), "Pong").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
35            std::io::stdout().flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
36        }
37        Commands::Exit => {
38            write!(std::io::stdout(), "Exiting ...").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
39            std::io::stdout().flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
40            return Ok(true);
41        }
42    }
43    Ok(false)
44}
```

}## Expand description

Parse a sub-command into a user-defined enum.

Implementing this trait lets a parent container delegate subcommand behavior to `Self`.
with:

- `#[command(subcommand)] field: SubCmd`: Attribute can be used with either struct fields or enum variants that impl- `Subcommand`.
- `#[command(flatten)] Variant(SubCmd)`: Attribute can only be used with enum variants that impl- `Subcommand`.

**NOTE:** Deriving requires the `derive` feature flag

# condtype 1.3.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/condtype/1.3.0

`condtype`

Choose Rust types at compile-time via boolean constants, brought to you by
[Nikolai Vazquez](https://hachyderm.io/@nikolai).

If you find this library useful, consider
[starring it](https://github.com/nvzqz/condtype) as well as
[sponsoring](https://github.com/sponsors/nvzqz) or
[donating once](https://paypal.me/nvzqz). 💖

## Conditional Typing

The [ CondType](https://docs.rs/condtype/latest/condtype/type.CondType.html) type and

[macro choose types at compile-time using](https://docs.rs/condtype/latest/condtype/macro.condval.html)

`condval!`[constants, just like](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.bool.html)

`bool`[. Unlike the](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/conditional)

`std::conditional_t` in C++[type, the type chosen by](https://docs.rs/either/latest/either/enum.Either.html)

`Either`[/](https://docs.rs/condtype/latest/condtype/type.CondType.html)

`CondType`[is directly used, rather than wrapped with an](https://docs.rs/condtype/latest/condtype/macro.condval.html)

`condval!`[type. This may be considered a form of](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/keyword.enum.html)

`enum`[dependent typing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependent_type), but it is limited in ability and is restricted to compile-time constants rather than runtime values.

`CondType`

In the following example, [ CondType](https://docs.rs/condtype/latest/condtype/type.CondType.html) aliases either

[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html)

`&str`[, depending on the boolean](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.i32.html)

`i32`[generic constant](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/generics.html#const-generics):

```
use CondType;
let str:  = "hello";
let int:  = 42;
// Unsized types are also supported:
let str: & = "world";
```
`condval!`

[ condval!](https://docs.rs/condtype/latest/condtype/macro.condval.html) enables choosing differently-typed values without specifying types.
In the following example,

`val` is inferred to be either [or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.str.html)

`&str`[, depending on](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.i32.html)

`i32``COND`.```
use condval;
const COND: bool = true;
let val = condval!;
assert_eq!;
```
`if let` pattern matching is also supported:

```
use condval;
const STR:  = Some;
let val = condval!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Platform-Specific Types

This library can make code for some platforms more efficient by using smaller-sized types, depending on platform-specific constants.

In the following example, the `RlimOption` type can be either
[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html)<[rlim_t](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/sys_resource.h.html)> or [ rlim_t](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/sys_resource.h.html) itself,
where

[can be treated as a sentinel value for](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.u64.html#associatedconstant.MAX)

`rlim_t::MAX`[if it is not equal to](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`Option::None`[.](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/sys_resource.h.html)

`RLIM_INFINITY````
use ;
use ;
const RLIM_INFINITY_IS_MAX: bool = RLIM_INFINITY == rlim_tMAX;
type RlimOption = ;
const RLIM_NONE: RlimOption = condval!;
// Convert from either `RlimOption` type to `Option` via the `Into` trait:
let rlim_none:  = RLIM_NONE.into;
```
Without this library, one could otherwise use [ cfg_if!](https://docs.rs/cfg-if/latest/cfg_if/macro.cfg_if.html) to achieve the same
goal. However, using

[requires maintaining a list of platforms and being more fine-grained if](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rust-by-example/attribute/cfg.html)

`#[cfg]`[is dependent on CPU architecture.](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/sys_resource.h.html)

`RLIM_INFINITY````
use cfg_if;
use rlim_t;
cfg_if!
```
## Limitations

It is currently not possible to use [ CondType](https://docs.rs/condtype/latest/condtype/type.CondType.html) or

[with a](https://docs.rs/condtype/latest/condtype/macro.condval.html)

`condval!`[generic constant](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/generics.html#const-generics)because

[Rust does not yet consider trait implementations based on booleans to be exhaustive](https://github.com/rust-lang/project-const-generics/issues/26). Once that issue is resolved, all versions of this library should

*just work*with generic constants.

```
```

# condtype - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/condtype/1.3.0/target-redirect/condtype/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#condtype)`condtype`

Choose Rust types at compile-time via boolean constants, brought to you by
[Nikolai Vazquez](https://hachyderm.io/@nikolai).

If you find this library useful, consider
[starring it](https://github.com/nvzqz/condtype) as well as
[sponsoring](https://github.com/sponsors/nvzqz) or
[donating once](https://paypal.me/nvzqz). 💖

[§](https://docs.rs#conditional-typing)Conditional Typing

The [ CondType](https://docs.rs/type.CondType.html) type and

[macro choose types at compile-time using](https://docs.rs/macro.condval.html)

`condval!`[constants, just like](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`bool`[. Unlike the](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/types/conditional)

`std::conditional_t` in C++[type, the type chosen by](https://docs.rs/either/latest/either/enum.Either.html)

`Either`[/](https://docs.rs/type.CondType.html)

`CondType`[is directly used, rather than wrapped with an](https://docs.rs/macro.condval.html)

`condval!`[type. This may be considered a form of](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/keyword.enum.html)

`enum`[dependent typing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dependent_type), but it is limited in ability and is restricted to compile-time constants rather than runtime values.

[§](https://docs.rs#condtype-1)`CondType`

In the following example, [ CondType](https://docs.rs/type.CondType.html) aliases either

[or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)

`&str`[, depending on the boolean](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)

`i32`[generic constant](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/generics.html#const-generics):

```
use condtype::CondType;
let str: CondType<true,  &str, i32> = "hello";
let int: CondType<false, &str, i32> = 42;
// Unsized types are also supported:
let str: &CondType<true, str, [u8]> = "world";
```
[§](https://docs.rs#condval)`condval!`

[ condval!](https://docs.rs/macro.condval.html) enables choosing differently-typed values without specifying types.
In the following example,

`val` is inferred to be either [or](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)

`&str`[, depending on](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i32.html)

`i32``COND`.```
use condtype::condval;
const COND: bool = true;
let val = condval!(if COND {
    "hello"
} else {
    42
});
assert_eq!(val, "hello");
```
`if let` pattern matching is also supported:

```
use condtype::condval;
const STR: Option<&str> = Some("hello");
let val = condval!(if let Some(str) = STR {
    str.to_uppercase()
} else {
    42
});
assert_eq!(val, "HELLO");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#platform-specific-types)Platform-Specific Types

This library can make code for some platforms more efficient by using smaller-sized types, depending on platform-specific constants.

In the following example, the `RlimOption` type can be either
[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[rlim_t](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/sys_resource.h.html)>[ rlim_t](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/sys_resource.h.html) itself,
where

[can be treated as a sentinel value for](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html#associatedconstant.MAX)

`rlim_t::MAX`[if it is not equal to](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`Option::None`[.](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/sys_resource.h.html)

`RLIM_INFINITY````
use condtype::{condval, CondType};
use libc::{rlim_t, RLIM_INFINITY};
const RLIM_INFINITY_IS_MAX: bool = RLIM_INFINITY == rlim_t::MAX;
type RlimOption = CondType<RLIM_INFINITY_IS_MAX, Option<rlim_t>, rlim_t>;
const RLIM_NONE: RlimOption = condval!(if RLIM_INFINITY_IS_MAX {
    None::<rlim_t>
} else {
    rlim_t::MAX
});
// Convert from either `RlimOption` type to `Option` via the `Into` trait:
let rlim_none: Option<rlim_t> = RLIM_NONE.into();
```
Without this library, one could otherwise use [ cfg_if!](https://docs.rs/cfg-if/latest/cfg_if/macro.cfg_if.html) to achieve the same
goal. However, using

[requires maintaining a list of platforms and being more fine-grained if](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rust-by-example/attribute/cfg.html)

`#[cfg]`[is dependent on CPU architecture.](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/sys_resource.h.html)

`RLIM_INFINITY````
use cfg_if::cfg_if;
use libc::rlim_t;
cfg_if! {
    // Platforms where `RLIM_INFINITY != rlim_t::MAX`:
    if #[cfg(any(
        target_os = "macos",
        target_os = "freebsd",
        target_os = "solaris",
        // ad nauseam...
    ))] {
        type RlimOption = rlim_t;
        const RLIM_NONE: RlimOption = rlim_t::MAX;
    } else {
        type RlimOption = Option<rlim_t>;
        const RLIM_NONE: RlimOption = None;
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#limitations)Limitations

It is currently not possible to use [ CondType](https://docs.rs/type.CondType.html) or

[with a](https://docs.rs/macro.condval.html)

`condval!`[generic constant](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/generics.html#const-generics)because

[Rust does not yet consider trait implementations based on booleans to be exhaustive](https://github.com/rust-lang/project-const-generics/issues/26). Once that issue is resolved, all versions of this library should

*just work*with generic constants.

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn generic<const B: bool>() {
    let val: CondType<B, &str, i32> = condval!(if B {
        "hello"
    } else {
        42
    });
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#install)Install

This library is [available on crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/condtype) and
can be used by running the following `cargo` command in your project directory:

`cargo add condtype`or by manually adding the following to your project’s [ Cargo.toml](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html):

```
[dependencies]
condtype = "1.3.0"
```

Like the Rust project, this library may be used under either the
[MIT License](https://github.com/nvzqz/condtype/blob/main/LICENSE-MIT) or
[Apache License (Version 2.0)](https://github.com/nvzqz/condtype/blob/main/LICENSE-APACHE).
